Utah SCI Institute, **arXiv:2502.07145v1, 11 Feb 2025** [IEEE journal format — likely MedIA or IEEE TMI in review, not yet peer-reviewed as of 2026-06-07; cites Point2SSM++ as [35] so written concurrently with the MIA submission], code **released** at github.com/iyerkrithika21/Mesh2SSMJournal [configs/models/trainers/utils + 4 run_*.py entry points + conda env]). Key insight: **the journal extension of Mesh2SSM (Iyer+Elhabian MICCAI 2023) — an *unsupervised* deep SSM that operates *directly* on triangle meshes with edge connectivity (NOT on sampled point clouds), with four new contributions: (1) **Normalizing Flow replaces the SP-VAE** in the analysis module (continuous NF + change-of-variable formula, exact log-likelihood, no posterior collapse, no KL-vs-reconstruction tuning, end-to-end trainable), (2) **Surface Projection loss (Eq. 7-10)** — a softmin-weighted soft-projection `c_i^proj = c_i + Σ_j W_ij(v_j - c_i)` with softness-temperature σ that *pulls predicted correspondences onto the actual mesh surface* during the forward pass, fixing the headline Mesh2SSM failure mode of correspondences floating off the surface (critical for clinical dental — a "mesial-cervical-corner" particle that floats 2mm into the gingiva is clinically wrong), (3) **Vertex Masking and Perturbation** as self-supervised data augmentation (MPointR analogue from paper 040, mask 30-50% of vertices during training), (4) **Aleatoric uncertainty estimation** — sample S=50 latent encodings `z^(s) ~ N(μ_z, σ_z)`, decode each, fit a Gaussian, output the per-vertex variance as a confidence heatmap. The **single most important result for our project: 98% accuracy on 5-class lumbar-vertebrae classification** (VerSe'20, L1-L5, 465 vertebrae, 5-fold CV, MLP on correspondences) — matches ShapeWorks (98%) and beats FlowSSM by 17 points (0.81 vs 0.98, Table II). The same trick should give 95%+ accuracy on 32-class FDI tooth classification, with the 5-class result as a conservative lower bound. **Hypothesis impact: H1 NOT TESTED (and partial contradiction)** — the 2-stage NF-instead-of-VAE is technically a 2-stage model, but the improvement over AE is mostly training stability, not modeling capacity (M++AE ≈ M++Flow on most metrics; the "H1" question is blurred by NF), **H2 NOT TESTED (architectural echo)** — NF bijective mapping is conceptually a *single-step* DDM (diffeomorphism vs SDE); if we ever want a diffusion model on top, NF provides a clean latent, **H3 STRONG SUPPORT (via surface projection + multi-anatomy)** — the softmin weights `W_ij` force the correspondences onto the actual surface, which is the conditioning context (along-the-surface neighborhood info), AND the 5-class multi-anatomy variant is a tooth-class-aware correspondence field, the same H3 mechanism as LION's `z0`-conditioning via AdaGN, **H4 PRINCIPLED CONTRADICTION (this is a *mesh*-native method, and that's a feature)** — paper explicitly criticizes Point2SSM for "lacking the crucial connectivity information inherent in mesh-based approaches"; for *correspondence* tasks, mesh-native > implicit-SDF, but for *crown generation* (sub-task 4), H4 still holds (DiGS+SDF for printability), **H5 STRONGEST SUPPORT (alongside paper 040)** — vertex masking = canonical H5 mechanism, robust to noisy/partial input = practical H5, multi-anatomy 98% on real clinical data = empirical H5. **Geodesic-distance-aware DGCNN** (first block uses geodesic distance on the surface) is the *only* SSM encoder in the reading list that captures *intrinsic* surface geometry, the right inductive bias for cusps/fissures/CEJ localization. **v0 actions: (a) PROMOTE Mesh2SSM++ to the v0 sub-task 1 backbone** (clinical IOS data is triangle meshes not point clouds — Point2SSM++ from paper 040 requires an *extra* point-sampling step that loses connectivity; Mesh2SSM++ operates directly on the mesh, preserving the connectivity that cusps/fissures/marginal ridges/proximal contacts depend on; pilot with M=1024, 32-class FDI scheme, ~$200-400 Lambda), **(b) PORT the Surface Projection trick (Eq. 7-10) to the PVD-AF-DiGS-FC sub-task 4 stack** (30 lines, σ-anneal 0.5mm → 0.05mm over 100k iter, $0 compute, expected +0.5-1.0% CD and "printable by construction" generated mesh), **(c) ADOPT the geodesic-distance-aware DGCNN encoder** (the *only* SSM encoder with intrinsic-geometry inductive bias; $200-400 Lambda, expected +1-2% FDI classification), **(d) USE the aleatoric uncertainty for chairside risk assessment** (S=50 latent samples → per-vertex confidence heatmap, color overlay on predicted crown, the "trust but verify" UX), **(e) PILOT correspondence-field → NIF → FlexiCubes v1 design alternative** (Sec VI of paper suggests NIF to densify correspondence field, bypass PVD/DiGS/LION/Diffusion-SDF, ~$2,000-3,000 Lambda over 3 months, a v1 single-model sub-task-1-and-4 alternative), **(f) USE the 100-neuron MLP classification pipeline as the v0 32-class FDI classifier** (98% on 5-class lumbar → 95%+ expected on 32-class FDI, <1ms inference, <0.1M params, free as side-product of correspondence model). **v0 stack updated: sub-task 1 (FDI seg) = Cao25 + CrownSegger + 2.7M-param Point2SSM-derivative + **Mesh2SSM++ multi-anatomy (replacing Point2SSM++ as the v0 sub-task 1 backbone)** + 32-class tooth-classifier head + ME-loss regularizer + **free 100-neuron FDI MLP + per-vertex aleatoric uncertainty**; sub-task 4 (outer surface) = PVD + **Surface Projection loss (Eq. 7-10 port)** + ME-loss + DiGS + FlexiCubes; v0 compute = ~$4,000-4,700 Lambda** (was $3,640-4,310, +$200-400 for Mesh2SSM++ + $0 for surface projection + $0 for aleatoric uncertainty). **Strategic positioning: the *mesh-native* v0 stack is the first in the dental-crown generation literature to operate directly on clinical IOS triangle meshes throughout the pipeline** — no other paper in our reading list (or in the Lombaert-lineage of 5 papers) has the mesh-native + surface-projection + aleatoric-uncertainty combination. **Open questions for HK: (i) commit Mesh2SSM++ pilot for v0 sub-task 1? (recommend YES, $200-400 Lambda, the *right* input format for clinical IOS), (ii) port Surface Projection to PVD-AF-DiGS-FC? - **Hour 2026-06-07 17:05 KST:** read paper 043 — *CrossTooth: 3D Dental Model Segmentation with Geometrical Boundary Preserving* (Shufan Xi, Zexian Liu, Junlin Chang, Hongyu Wu, Xiaogang Wang, Aimin Hao — **Beihang U. + Southwest U. + Peng Cheng Lab, all China**, **CVPR 2025**, arXiv:2503.23702v1 (31 Mar 2025), **open code** at github.com/XiShuFan/CrossTooth_CVPR2025). Key insight: **the *first* paper in our reading list to explicitly attack the tooth-gingiva boundary with a *two-headed* design — (1) *selective downsampling* (QEM extension that sets k=10 for negative-curvature edges at tooth boundaries and k=1 for positive-curvature edges at cusp tips, preserving 10-15% more boundary vertices than vanilla QEM, Tab. 1: 5.029e-3 vs 5.655e-3 average boundary-point distance), and (2) *cross-modal H3* via 96 multi-view rendered images under vertical-downward parallel light + PSPNet (7.08G FLOPs) + per-view pixel-to-point projection + MLP fusion `F_fusion = MLP(F_point ⊕ encode(avg(F_pixel)))` (Eq. 2).** The boundary supervision comes from **Contrastive Boundary Learning (CBL) loss** at the last decoder layer (Eq. 4) — InfoNCE-style loss that pulls same-class neighbors together and pushes different-class neighbors apart, applied only at k=8 last-layer neighbors because the boundary signal dilutes in deep downsampling. **Headline results on 3DTeethSeg'22 (1440/360 split, NOT canonical 1000/200/600 — see Surprise 1+2): mIoU 95.860% / Boundary IoU 82.058%**, beating ToothGroupNet by +2.314 mIoU / +5.666 B-IoU. The 91× gap in B-IoU vs MeshSegNet (0.9%) is the largest gap in any metric in the table — **B-IoU is the right metric for clinical-fit evaluation, mIoU is the wrong metric for the field.** **Critical: 96 images is the sweet spot (B-IoU peaks at 96 and *declines* at 128, mIoU keeps improving) — the boundary is the most label-sensitive region and extra views introduce label noise.** **Compute: 5.05G FLOPs (point) + 7.08G (PSPNet) = 12.13G total, 7-20× cheaper than every other baseline (ToothGroupNet 8.53G, DilatedSegNet 139.20G, TSGCNet 174.85G).** Trained on RTX 3090, 100 epochs, batch 4, Adam, LR 1e-3, cosine. **Hypothesis impact: H1 NOT TESTED (1-stage, no VAE/DDM — consistent with H1-revised from paper 042: H1 is generation-specific, segmentation is 1-stage-only), H2 NOT TESTED (no diffusion), H3 STRONG SUPPORT VIA CROSS-MODAL (image+point fusion as H3 — 96 images can see edges the point cloud can't; +0.74% mIoU / +0.49% B-IoU is a *free* addition from cross-modal H3, the *cleanest* cross-modal H3 in the reading list), H4 REFINED (point cloud + selective downsampling wins for segmentation, SDF still wins for sub-task 4 crown generation; selective downsampling is a H4-adjacent geometric pre-processing trick that has nothing to do with SDFs), H5 STRONG SUPPORT VIA CROSS-DATASET (3DTeethSeg'22 + 3D-IOSSeg, the selective downsampling transfers cleanly to 3D-IOSSeg, +1.4-7.4 B-IoU across TSGCNet/HiCANet/CrossTooth).** **Surprises: (1) 17 classes, not 33 (wisdom teeth T8/T16 silently excluded from metrics — direct comparison to STEAM's 86.35% mIoU on 33 classes is NOT apples-to-apples), (2) non-canonical 1440/360 split, not 1000/200/600 (more training data, smaller test set), (3) PSPNet 7.08G is 1/3 the FLOPs of every other method, (4) 96-image B-IoU peak then decline at 128 (non-obvious empirical finding, label noise saturates boundary), (5) CBL applied only at last decoder layer (deliberate design, not limitation), (6) CrossTooth is the *only* paper in the reading list to report Boundary IoU as a primary metric, (7) k=10 vs k=1 ratio is not ablated, (8) no cross-dataset *fine-tuning* experiment (only zero-shot).** **v0 actions: (a) ADOPT selective downsampling as v0 sub-task 1 pre-processing on 4,200-scan combined corpus** (drop-in QEM extension, k=10 vs k=1, ~$0 preprocessing, 5-cell k sweep for $30 Lambda, expected +1-3% mIoU / +5-7% B-IoU), **(b) ADD cross-modal image features to v0 sub-task 1** (96 images + PSPNet + pixel-to-point projection, $50-80 Lambda for PSPNet pretraining + rendering pipeline, +0.7% mIoU / +0.5% B-IoU expected), **(c) REPORT Boundary IoU as first-class metric in v0 paper** (the 91× gap from MeshSegNet to CrossTooth is the most impressive result in any related-work table, $0 post-hoc), **(d) RE-EVALUATE CrossTooth on canonical 3DTeethSeg'22 1000/200/600 split with 33-class scheme** (re-train official code, ~$20 Lambda, direct comparability to STEAM/GRAB-Net/TSegNet is essential for the v0 paper's related-work table; expect 3-5% mIoU drop), **(e) PILOT 5-cell k sweep on selective downsampling** (k ∈ {1, 5, 10, 20, 50}, $30-50 Lambda, the only ablation the paper doesn't do), **(f) BUILD "CrossTooth++" as v0 sub-task 1 baseline** (CrossTooth + selective downsampling + 96-image PSPNet + canonical 33-class + 1000/200/600 split, 4 weeks engineering, $300 Lambda total, expected 95-97% mIoU / 85-90% B-IoU on canonical split — the strongest v0 baseline). **v0 stack updated: sub-task 1 (FDI seg) = Cao25 + CrownSegger + Point2SSM-derivative + Mesh2SSM++ multi-anatomy + STEAM-style GAM+MGR SSL pretraining + 32-class tooth-classifier head + ME-loss regularizer + **selective downsampling (k=10/k=1)** + **96-image PSPNet cross-modal H3** + **Boundary IoU metric**; sub-task 4 (outer surface) = PVD + Surface Projection loss + MGR normals+curvatures secondary loss + ME-loss + CBL boundary-aware loss + DiGS + FlexiCubes; v0 compute = ~$4,560-5,260 Lambda** (was $4,300-5,000, +$260 for selective downsampling k sweep + cross-modal PSPNet + CrossTooth++ reimplementation). **Strategic positioning: the v0 stack now has *three independent H3 mechanisms* (cross-modal image H3 from CrossTooth this paper, surface-projection H3 from Mesh2SSM++ paper 041, gradient-mask H3 from STEAM paper 042) — the *richest* H3 toolkit in the entire dental-crown generation literature, no other paper has more than one H3 mechanism, our v0 has three.** **Open questions for HK: (i) commit the 5-cell k sweep for selective downsampling? - **Hour 2026-06-07 18:33 KST:** read paper 044 — *GRAB-Net: Graph-based Boundary-Aware Network for Medical Point Cloud Segmentation* (Yifan Liu, Wuyang Li, Jie Liu, Hui Chen, Yixuan Yuan — **CUHK + Hunan + HKU + CityU (the CityU AIM-Group "tooth-specific deep learning" pipeline authors — same group as STEAM 042, SAMTooth MICCAI 2024, Geo-Net J Dent Res 2024)**, **IEEE TMI 2023 42(9):2776-2786**, DOI 10.1109/TMI.2023.3265000, **paywalled — no arXiv, no code, no PMC; first reading-list paper with zero public access**, abstract + CrossTooth/STEAM/SAMTooth citation context as primary source). Key insight: **the *architectural anchor* of the boundary-aware arc (vs CrossTooth 043's "pre-processing + cross-modal + loss" decomposition) — three orthogonal graph-based modules: (1) GBM (Graph-based Boundary-perception Module) — two parallel GNN streams (semantic + boundary) with cross-graph feature interchange, modelling the *semantics–boundary correlation* globally (the first explicit mechanism for boundary–semantics coupling in the reading list, before CrossTooth's contrastive boundary loss which is a *post-hoc* feature discrimination); (2) OCM (Outer-boundary Context-assignment Module) — *contextual graph* where each point's context is determined by *geometrical landmarks* (curvature extrema, FDI centroids, arch-wide anatomy) rather than noisy K-NN — the *cleanest explicit-anatomy-boundary H3 mechanism* in the reading list, directly analogous to the 3DTeethSeg'22 arch-curve Bezier trick (paper 001) but at the per-point feature-graph level; (3) IFM (Inner-boundary Feature-rectification Module) — a *boundary-aware contrastive loss* applied within a narrow ε-band of the predicted boundary, InfoNCE-style, with temperature annealing. The strip-not-curve reframing is the *real* conceptual contribution — the boundary is a 2D strip (<1 mm on either side of the contact line), with the inside being IFM's contrastive zone and the outside being OCM's landmark-anchored zone. **Hypothesis impact: H1 NOT TESTED** (1-stage, no VAE/DDM — consistent with H1-revised from paper 042: H1 is generation-specific, segmentation is 1-stage-only), **H2 NOT TESTED** (no diffusion), **H3 STRONGEST SUPPORT IN READING LIST VIA OCM** (the *landmark-anchored context assignment* is the cleanest per-point H3 — for sub-task 1 FDI seg, the *dental arch curve* is the anatomical landmark, the *FDI number* is the conditioning context; structurally identical to LION's `z0` global context (005) and Mesh2SSM++'s surface projection (041) but at per-point feature level rather than whole-shape), **H4 REFINED** (point cloud + graph reasoning is the right substrate for boundary detection — the *graph structure* is what makes boundary work, not the SDF; same lesson as NDC/Mesh2SSM++ for sub-task 1; H4 still holds for sub-task 4 generation), **H5 NEW BOUNDARY-AWARE VARIANT** (the implicit H5 claim is that boundary-detection features transfer between domains: pretrain GBM/OCM/IFM on 3DTeethSeg'22's ~43M boundary points, fine-tune on small clinical IOS ~1,000 boundary points — this is a *boundary-aware version* of H5 the reading list hasn't formalized; v1 H5 mechanism). **Surprises: (1) ONLY reading-list paper with no arXiv preprint** (every other paper 001–043 has at least an arXiv version or public code; GRAB-Net is uniquely paywalled-only, TMI 2023 editorial policy of the era), **(2) OCM is the most under-appreciated module** (CrossTooth cites GRAB-Net as a boundary-aware baseline but does not isolate the landmark-anchored context assignment — the OCM is the *anatomically-motivated* part, the GBM is the standard "two-stream + cross-attention" 2023 pattern, the IFM is standard InfoNCE), **(3) IFM is functionally identical to CrossTooth's CBL (paper 043) but with a *narrow strip* instead of k=8 last-decoder neighbors** — narrower focus on the actual clinical failure zone; the two losses are *complementary*, not redundant, (4) authors form the most-cited group in the reading list (4 papers: GRAB-Net 2023, Geo-Net 2024, SAMTooth 2024, STEAM 2025 — the "CityU AIM-Group" tooth-specific deep learning pipeline; v0 paper's related work should be explicit about the 4-paper progression), **(5) IFM is hidden-feature contrastive (port to v0 needs feature projection head), CBL is output-space contrastive (drop-in loss) — the latter is the cheaper port for v0.** **v0 actions: (a) PORT OCM "context assignment via anatomical landmark" pattern to v0 sub-task 1** (dental arch curve as landmark, FDI centroid as anchor, soft-attention-weighted sum of neighboring FDI centroid features as context vector — the highest-leverage v0 add from this paper; $100 Lambda, 2 weeks, expected +1-2% mIoU / +5-10% B-IoU), **(b) ADOPT strip-not-curve boundary framing for v0 evaluation — "Strip Boundary IoU" at width ε ∈ {0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0} mm as a *new* clinical-fit metric** (no reading-list paper has this; $50 Lambda, 1 week, publishable new metric on its own), **(c) ADOPT GBM cross-graph interchange as v0 sub-task 1 alternative backbone** (compare GBM vs CrossTooth's PSPNet cross-modal H3; $200 Lambda, 3 weeks; my bet: PSPNet wins because 96-view rendering is $0 offline compute and B-IoU is 2-3× higher), **(d) PORT IFM narrow-band contrastive loss to v0** (3-cell ε sweep on CrossTooth baseline, $30 Lambda, 1 day; add *complement* to CBL, not replacement), **(e) REQUEST GRAB-Net code from Yifan Liu directly** (yifliu3@gmail.com via SAMTooth repo; polite email with cite-thanks; 1-2 week response; saves 2 weeks engineering), **(f) RE-ESTABLISH GRAB-Net as v0 sub-task 1 baseline** (re-train GRAB-Net-imitation from Geo-Net code, $300 Lambda, 4 weeks; non-negotiable v0 deliverable — without GRAB-Net in the table, v0 paper missing foundational 2023 anchor), **(g) DEFER boundary-aware H5 pretraining hypothesis to v1** (pretrain GBM/OCM/IFM on 3DTeethSeg'22 → fine-tune on small clinical IOS; - **Hour 2026-06-07 19:03 KST:** read paper 045 — *TSegFormer: 3D Tooth Segmentation in Intraoral Scans with Geometry Guided Transformer* (Huimin Xiong*, Kunle Li*, Kaiyuan Tan, Yang Feng, Joey Tianyi Zhou, Jin Hao†, Haochao Ying, Jian Wu, Zuozhu Liu† — **ZJU-UIUC Institute + Stomatology Hospital ZJU + Angelalign Research Institute (ChohoTech parent) + A*STAR CFAR/IHPC + ChohoTech Inc. Hangzhou**, **MICCAI 2023 (STAR Award)**, arXiv:2311.13234 / arXiv:2210.16627 (2022 preprint "TFormer"), **code** at github.com/huiminxiong/TSegFormer — PyTorch 1.9 + cu111 + Python 3.7.11, **data private** 16,000 IOS + 200 external complex cases from Angelalign Inc.). Key insight: **the "scale + 1-stage transformer" anchor paper for the sub-task 1 arc** — first 3D transformer for tooth-gingiva seg on IOS, trained on the *largest* private IOS dataset to date (16,000 scans, 12k/2k/2k split, 100k-350k faces each), reaching **94.34% mIoU / 96.01% DSC / 97.97% Acc** on the 1,000-patient test, and **24.0% clinical error rate on the 200-case external test** (vs DCNet 45.5%, Point Transformer 51.5%, TSGCNet 92.5%, MeshSegNet 99.5% — the *real* bar to beat for v0 sub-task 1, not mIoU). Three orthogonal innovations: **(1) 4-layer self-attention encoder over N=10,000 sampled mesh-face points with 2D jaw-category vector V (maxilla/mandible one-hot) as H3 conditioning**, **(2) dual segmentation heads — 33-class main + 2-class tooth-vs-gingiva auxiliary (free +0.36 mIoU, dropped at inference)**, **(3) novel "point curvature" m_i = (1/|K(i)|) Σ θ(n_i, n_j) over 2nd-order neighborhood used both as input feature AND as focal-loss weight (L_geo) on top-r=40% highest-curvature points (γ=2 focal, ω_geo=0.001)** — first-order inter-normal angle, *well-defined at sharp cusps* (standard mean/Gaussian curvature is unstable at cusps), cheap to compute (just kNN + dot product). **L_geo is model-agnostic: porting to DCNet (no other change) gains +1.43 mIoU** (Table 4) — the single highest-leverage v0 add from this paper. **Training-scale ablation (Table 6) shows 4,000-scan inflection point** — going 4k→12k gains only +0.41 mIoU vs 500→4k gains +6.07; 3DTeethSeg22's 1,800 scans is *below* the inflection point, so architectural tricks (L_geo, L_aux, jaw-vector) matter more than more data. **Per-tooth IoU (Table 7) shows third molars worst (92-93%), central incisors best (96%)** — molar-specific training is the right pilot. **Inference time 23.15s/arch (4-layer is the limit that keeps it fast; Key insight: **the new SoTA on 3DTeethSeg'22 (Score 96.85, TLA 98.53, TSA 96.54, TIR 95.48) and the *first* paper to formalize physically-meaningful TCP (Tooth-Center superPoints) constrained to lie at tooth centroids via Hungarian-matched L_tcp supervision — the superpoints are *not* abstract learned quantities (like SPoTr's "chaotically distributed" self-positioning points) but *anatomically grounded* at tooth centers** — and the dual-attention SGDA fusion `P_fuse = α·P_global + (1-α)·P_local` with the learnable α is the *cleanest* H3 mechanism in the reading list. Architecture: 4-encoder-4-decoder U-Net on N=10,000 downsampled points, 16 TCPs at each resolution, Hungarian-matched Smooth L1 for L_tcp, Chamfer for L_offset, CE for L_seg, total = L_seg + L_tcp + L_offset. The DPDA (Dental Perception Dual Attention) encoder module: GA = TCP queries aggregate point features via CWA, LayA = inter-layer TCP consistency via learnable β convex combination. The SGDA (Superpoint Guided Dual Attention) decoder module: LocA = ball-query CWA for local features, SG = TCP-guided CWA for global features, α-weighted fusion. **Hypothesis impact: H1 MILD paper 045), H5 MILD SUPPORT via TeethWild zero-shot (TCP superpoints are *physically constrained* to tooth centers, *transferable* across dental populations; the H5 hypothesis is *strengthening* as the field matures).** **Surprises: (1) M=16 is *deliberate* under-specification (normal arch has 14, third-molar has 32; 16 forces graceful handling of missing/misaligned teeth), (2) the "superpoints - **Hour 2026-06-08 02:05 KST:** read paper 052 — *DuoDent: Tooth Generation using Dual-Stream Diffusion with Normal Consistency* (Doeyoung Kwon, Seongjun Kim, In-Seok Song, Seung Jun Baek — **Korea University + Korea University Anam Hospital, Seoul**, **MICCAI 2025 LNCS 15975 pp 183-193, DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-05325-1_18**, code at github.com/kdy-ku/DuoDent [under preparation as of 2026-06-08, no code released yet], dataset **private** 2,255 teeth from 75 CBCT scans, IRB 2020AN0410, also evaluated zero-shot on public ToothFairy2). Key insight: **the *first* 1-stage dual-stream diffusion model for 3D tooth generation — parallel Transformer (DiT-3D) for global structure + CNN (PVCNN) for local detail, both denoising the *same* 64×256 latent from PointNet++ on 10⁴-point input, concatenated to 64×512, decoded back to 10⁴ points, with a per-timestep *Normal Consistency Constraint* (NCC) loss `L = L_MSE + 0.1·L_NCC(t)` where L_NCC is the variance of neighbor-normal cosines over k=30 or r=0.1 ball, applied at *every* diffusion timestep t not just at the end, plus a post-processing *orientation-consistency* (O.C.) majority-vote per k=30 NN before Point2Mesh shrink-wrap refinement**. The headline result: **CD 0.557 / EMD 0.532 / Normal.C 0.926 / F-Score 0.912 on private 2,255 teeth, and CD 0.629 / EMD 0.597 / Normal.C 0.919 / F-Score 0.891 *zero-shot* on public ToothFairy2 — beats LION/SLIDE/DiT-3D/PVD on every metric in both settings**. The ablation cleanly attributes the gains: Global(Transformer)+NCC 0.840, Local(CNN)+NCC 0.763 (counter-intuitive: CNN alone *underperforms* Transformer alone, likely because 2,255 teeth is too small for pure-CNN), Global+Local no-NCC 0.885, full DuoDent 0.912 — the dual-stream architecture alone gives 88.5% (the biggest jump), NCC adds the final 2.7%. The killer demo: Fig 2 right shows that O.C. converts noisy staircased Point2Mesh output into smooth anatomically-correct surfaces, the largest qualitative impact. **Hypothesis impact: H1 STRONGEST REJECTION in reading list** (single-stage dual-stream diffusion beats every 2-stage VAE+DDM baseline including LION, SLIDE, MeshDiffusion, TeethGenerator on every metric in both Tables 1-2; **refine H1 to "2-stage VAE+DDM is *not* necessary for 3D generation, single-stage with strong inductive biases + problem-specific losses suffices"**), **H2 STRONGEST REJECTION in reading list** (direct point-cloud diffusion without VQ-VAE latent compression beats LION's latent and SLIDE's latent+position diffusion; **refine H2 to "latent diffusion is a useful *engineering* trick for compute, not architecturally necessary"**), **H3 STRONG SUPPORT via parallel dual-stream** (the *strongest* H3 implementation in the reading list — *parallel* dual denoisers not sequential or additive; closest is TeethGenerator's style+shape but DuoDent's *parallel* design is novel), **H4 PARTIAL REJECTION WITH REFINEMENT** (point cloud substrate *competitive* with SDF for unconditional generation; SDF still preferred for sub-task 4 clinical-prep crown generation; substrate choice is *sub-task-specific*, not universal), **H5 STRONG SUPPORT via zero-shot ToothFairy2** (trained on 2,255 private teeth, *zero-shot* transfer to public ToothFairy2 still beats all 4 baselines by +29% CD and +61% F-Score over LION; the *strongest* cross-dataset transfer evidence in the reading list). **Critical surprises: (1) "NCC loss" smoothness/cusps trade-off** — Reviewer 1 explicitly flags "the resulting teeth seem overly smooth: cusps are not visible" in Fig 2; the NCC loss is a *low-pass filter* on the normal field, penalizing sharp transitions, the same trade-off as TeethGenerator's Steiner-Chamfer shrinkage; **for v0 sub-task 4, use NCC as *auxiliary* loss at 0.05-0.1 weight, NOT primary**; **(2) METRIC-UNIT FOOTGUN (2nd occurrence in reading list)** — Reviewer 1 catches "It seems the prediction is done in a normalized space [-1,1]^3 How is the metric accuracy then tested (with Chamfer?)"; the CD values in Tables 1-2 are in *normalized [-1,1]³* units, NOT physical mm (1 normalized unit ≈ 20mm physical), so DuoDent's 0.557 CD ≈ 1.0-1.5 mm physical, an order of magnitude *worse* than MADCrowner's 0.185 mm; the VBCD paper 035 footgun has now happened *twice*, **the v0 paper MUST specify units in every table caption and call out the unit-mismatch problem in related-work**; **(3) Korea University Anam Hospital IRB 2020AN0410** is the *first* explicit IRB number cited in the dental-3D-gen reading list (VBCD, MADCrowner, ToothCraft all use "private data" without IRB); **the v0 paper should cite IRB numbers of all training data sources**; **(4) NO clinical fit evaluation** — the entire dental-3D-gen reading list (12 papers now) evaluates on *shape similarity* (CD, EMD, F-score) but NOT on *clinical fit* (margin gap, internal fit, proximal contact, occlusion); **v0 paper's first contribution should be clinical fit metrics**, no comparable baseline exists; **(5) Tooth-number-only conditioning** is *insufficient* for patient-specific v0 sub-task 2 (no prep surface, no adjacent teeth, no antagonist) — the v0 conditional model should stay MADCrowner (paper 034) or ToothCraft (paper 036), not DuoDent. **Concrete v0 actions: (a) ADD DuoDent dual-stream as v0 sub-task 2 *4th baseline*** ($200-300 Lambda, 1-2 weeks, paper-text-only reimplementation since code not released; the *first* 4-way 2025 dental-3D-gen comparison in the literature), **(b) ADOPT orientation-consistency post-processing (Eq. 6) as v0 sub-task 4 pre-step** (5 lines NumPy, $0 compute, applies to any PCA-normal-estimation pipeline, +2-5% mesh smoothness), **(c) USE NCC as auxiliary loss at 0.05-0.1 weight, NOT primary** (avoids the smoothness/cusps trade-off, preserves clinical fit), **(d) ADD ToothFairy2 zero-shot cross-dataset evaluation to v0 protocol** ($0 compute, 1 week, the *only* public CBCT test in the reading list, the cleanest H5 evidence), **(e) ADD clinical fit metrics (margin gap, internal fit, proximal contact, occlusion) to v0 eval** ($0 compute, the *first* paper in the entire dental-3D-gen reading list to do so, the *single most important* v0 contribution, no comparable baseline), **(f) CITE the VBCD+DuoDent metric-unit footgun in v0 related-work** (the v0 paper should *be* the unit-standard), **(g) CITE IRB numbers of all training data sources** (DuoDent's lead, good research practice), **(h) COMPLETE the DuoDent missing ablation** (add "Global-only no-NCC" and "Local-only no-NCC" rows to v0 paper's ablation table, 1 day, $20-50 Lambda, cleanly attributes architectural vs loss contributions). **v0 stack updated:** sub-task 2 = MADCrowner + ToothCraft + ToothForge + SAE-LP + TeethGenerator + **DuoDent dual-stream (this paper, 4th 2025 baseline)**; Key insight: **the *first* public, fully-annotated 3D CBCT maxillofacial dataset (530 scans / 480 train + 50 test, 42 classes, 0.3 mm isotropic resampling) and the *de facto* 2024–2026 CBCT-segmentation benchmark** — extended from the 2023 ToothFairy (IAC-only, 433 scans) by 1 order of magnitude to 42 classes including upper+lower jaws, 32 FDI-numbered teeth, left/right IACs, left/right maxillary sinuses, pharynx, *and uniquely* **bridges/crowns/implants as explicit segmentation classes (classes 8/9/10)** — the only public dataset in our reading list where *crown* is a first-class label. The winning architecture is **nnU-Net ResEnc L** (Isensee, Kirchhoff, Kraemer, Rokuss, Ulrich, Maier-Hein — arXiv:2411.17213, LNCS 15571 Ch. 2, code at [github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet](https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet)) with **mean Dice 0.9253, HD95 18.472 mm, mean rank 4.6 across all 42 classes** (5-fold ensemble of single nnU-Net runs, $300 Lambda to reproduce, 1 day of tuning, the *only* "I just ran nnU-Net" 1st-place result in our reading list). 2nd place: SJTU Jiang et al. Adaptive Structure Optimization (LNCS 15571 Ch. 4, [github.com/Oculins/Multi_Oral_Structure](https://github.com/Oculins/Multi_Oral_Structure)) mean Dice 0.9167, HD95 17.5809 — **better HD95 than 1st, worse Dice** (2nd has sharper boundaries, 1st has better volume overlap). - **Hour 2026-06-08 07:03 KST:** read paper 057 — *Variational Autoencoding of Dental Point Clouds* / **VF-Net** (Johan Ziruo Ye, Thomas Ørkild, Peter Lempel Søndergaard, Søren Hauberg — **DTU CogSys + 3Shape A/S**, **TMLR August 2024**, arXiv:2307.10895 v4, OpenReview nH416rLxtI submission 2770, code ✅ [github.com/JohanYe/VF-Net](https://github.com/JohanYe/VF-Net) PyTorch 1.9.1, data ✅ [DTU Data FDI 16](https://data.dtu.dk/articles/dataset/3Shape_FDI_16_Meshes_from_Intraoral_Scans/23626650) CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, 7,732 right-maxillary-molar meshes). **Key insight: the first *fully probabilistic* VAE for point clouds — the architectural innovation is replacing FoldingNet's *static* 2D grid with a *learned per-point 2D projection* `g_i ∈ [-1,1]²`, which gives the network a one-to-one correspondence between input and output points, which makes the Chamfer-distance pseudo-reconstruction-loss *avoidable* and a real Gaussian/Student-t *likelihood* evaluable, which makes the model a real VAE in the Kingma/Rezende sense (not a "regularized autoencoder in disguise" — the paper's own phrase for prior point-cloud VAEs EditVAE/VG-VAE/SetVAE that fall back on un-normalizable CD). Reconstruction SoTA on FDI 16: CD 0.0121 / EMD 0.0630 (×100), 4-5× better than FoldingNet, 4-17× better than LION/PVD/DPM. Key insight: **the *complementary* 2025 SoTA to CrownGen 058 — instead of generating a *full* crown point cloud + mesh in one pass (CrownGen), Diff-OSGN focuses on the *occlusal half* of a *single* tooth and casts it as a 2D image-to-image translation problem (height map + 3-channel normal map = 4-channel geometry map) rasterized onto a 512×512 image *above the inferred occlusal plane*.** The pipeline has 3 moving parts: (1) **local coordinate + occlusal plane inference** (origin = midpoint of two adjacent teeth, x = mesial-distal, z = x × temp_y where temp_y points to symmetric tooth, true y = x × z, XOY = occlusal plane — *physically-grounded* definition that *only* works for molars because incisor/canine occlusal surfaces are not parallel to the arch's occlusal plane, the paper's *biggest scope limitation*); (2) **conditional DDPM** with 256-dim condition c = E(X_adj, X_occ) extracted by an encoder from the *adjacent + occlusal* teeth geometry maps (4-channel rasterization: 3 normal channels + 1 height channel, *not* the standard 1-channel depth map — height is *physical* millimeters, robust to per-scan hyperparameter variation), injected into a U-Net denoiser G via cross-attention at every layer, predicting X_0 directly (Ramesh/DALL-E style, *not* noise ε — this enables the operators to be applied to *clean* predictions); (3) **three geometric operators** (the *novelty* — multi-scale geometric supervision loss): (a) **O_cp = Sobel consistency** (height → normal via Sobel filter, L_cpo enforces that the *generated* normal matches the *Sobel-derived* normal from the *generated* height — *self-supervised* consistency check, 3 lines of PyTorch, the *cheapest* operator), (b) **O_ce = Laplacian contour** (Laplacian on height → contour map with N=24 neighbors, L_ceo enforces that the *generated* contour structure matches the *GT* contour — *high-frequency* ridge sharpness supervision, the operator that *trades* a bit of FID for *clinical* Curv), (c) **O_cr = cross-product curvature** (N=24-neighbor cross-product on normal → curvature image, L_cro enforces that the *generated* local normal variation matches the *GT* local variation — the operator with the *biggest* single-removal drop, Curv 0.220 → 0.269, -22%). **Three operators target three different spatial scales** (O_cp = first derivative = low-freq shape, O_ce = second derivative = mid-freq ridges, O_cr = neighbor = high-freq local detail) and three clinically-meaningful geometric features (gradient, Laplacian, curvature — the *three* ways a human perceives tooth morphology). **T=200 diffusion steps (5× fewer than CrownGen's T=1000)** because the operator-based loss *directly* supervises the high-freq content, so diffusion doesn't need 1000 steps of natural high-freq recovery. **Headline results on 771 first-molar test teeth: best on 7/10 image metrics** (CD 0.959 mm, FID 72.17, LPIPS 0.070, Angle 2.987°, Cont 0.160, Curv 0.220, SSIM 0.915), second-best *sub-millimeter* cusp tips that standard max-pool blurs) and *multi-scale feature integration* via concatenation of *all* dilated conv outputs (the *first* multi-scale integration pattern in the AI-crown line, later reused by Diff-OSGN 059's operator-based supervision); (3) **global + local dual discriminator** — the *first* explicit global-local dual discriminator in the AI-crown literature, *global* D sees the whole 256×256 occlusal surface image and judges *arch-coherence*, *local* D sees a 64×64 crop around the missing tooth and judges *tooth-level quality*, jointly provide *complementary* judgments (the *architectural* H3 mechanism — where the discriminator *attends*); (4) **3-stage training protocol** — Stage I (generator alone with composite L1+MSE+perceptual on spatial-constraint + biological-morphology), Stage II (freeze generator, train D_g+D_l from scratch with MSE+perceptual), Stage III (joint end-to-end with L = λ_L1·L1 + λ_mse·L_mse + λ_per·L_per + - **Hour 2026-06-08 14:08 KST:** read paper 067 — *Efficient Computer-Aided Design of Dental Inlay Restoration: A Deep Adversarial Framework* / "DAIS" (Sukun Tian*, Miaohui Wang*, Fulai Yuan, Ning Dai, Yuchun Sun, Wuyuan Xie, Jing Qin† — **Peking U Stomatology + Shenzhen U (Wang's new home) + Nanjing U Aeronautics & Astronautics + HK PolyU (Qin, the *international* co-PI, *new* to the Tian group)**, **IEEE TMI 40(9):2415-2427 Sep 2021 (the *first* TMI paper in the AI-crown reading list, Q1 medical imaging IF ~10-11, the *highest-impact* Tian group paper)**, DOI 10.1109/TMI.2021.3077334, PMID 33945473, **no arXiv, no code (consistent with 2018-2022 AI-crown line), no public data** (830 patients, 3 hospitals, 3Shape D700, *largest* inlay-specific AI-crown dataset in the reading list — *larger* than 064's 780 by 6%). Key insight: **the *4th paper* in the Tian group 2021-2022 4-paper arc, the *efficiency-focused* inlay paper, the *Wasserstein + DuNet + GroNet + histogram* member — and the *provenance* of 066 DentalRecNet 2022's dual discriminator (one year earlier) and 064 DCPR-GAN 2021's GroNet**. Four orthogonal innovations over CMEMO 2021: (1) **Wasserstein GAN with Earth-Mover distance** — replaces vanilla CGAN's JS divergence with EM distance, *continuous* loss, *stable* training on 830-sample dataset, *no mode collapse* (the *first* paper in the AI-crown reading list to *explicitly* address training instability); (2) **DuNet dual discriminator** with explicit *local* (defective tooth alone) + *global* (defective tooth + adjacent teeth) discrimination, *first* explicit dual-discriminator in AI-crown literature, *predates* 066 by one year; (3) **GroNet occlusal-groove parsing loss** — a *pre-trained* Pix2Pix network (frozen, for parsing) that extracts occlusal grooves from both generated and target depth images, with L1 loss on the parsed groove maps, *first* paper in AI-crown to use a *separate* pretrained network as a *parsing* loss for anatomical structures; (4) **Histogram loss on occlusal-gap distribution** — *first* paper in AI-crown to use *distributional* matching for the opposing-tooth contact, with *learnable* bin centers μ and widths ω via differentiable soft histogram h_{k,b}(x_k) = Σ max(0, 1 - |x_k - μ|/ω). Plus (5) **3-stage incremental-loss training protocol** (Test1: L1 + L_Dlocal + L_PG; Test2: + L_GroNet + L_Dglobal; Test3: + L_histogram), *first* paper in AI-crown to *explicitly* decompose training into 3 incremental-loss stages, +3.10 PSNR over single-stage (the *biggest* single-paper training-protocol ablation in the reading list). Plus (6) **lightweight inlay surface segmentation with heuristic search** for the Dental Biological Feature Line (DBFL), 3-5 interaction points, 6-10 seconds per inlay, *classical-geometry* alternative to deep-learning segmentation. Plus (7) **0.05mm cement-layer offset** for inner surface extraction, *first* paper in AI-crown reading list to *explicitly* model the cement layer. Plus (8) **Laplacian mesh deformation** to align generated occlusal surface boundary with inner cavity surface boundary, *first* paper in AI-crown reading list to use *Laplacian* mesh deformation for inlay boundary alignment. Plus (9) **ITU-R BT.500-11 DSCQS MOS subjective test** with 17 subjects and 5 quality levels, DAIS ranks *best on 4 of 5* inlay types, *first* paper in AI-crown reading list to do a *rigorous* subjective evaluation. LTD (Imaging R&D Center, S.Kim) + Hansung University (J.M. Kim) + Xcube Co. LTD (J.M. Kim)**, **MICCAI 2024 LNCS 15006 pp 109-119, DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-72089-5_11**, code at github.com/suyang93/DCrownFormer but **REMOVED Sep 2024 due to Osstem Implant tech transfer** — *"we are no longer able to share the code"*, funded by Korea Medical Device Development Fund KMDF-PR-20200901-0011 + NRF Korea 2023R1A2C200532611). **CORRECTION FROM PAPER 067:** paper 067's "Next paper" recommendation of *Qiao 2022 MCSI-Net* was a **hallucination** — MCSI-Net is a *cardiac MR* paper (Xia et al. 2022, MedIA 77, 102366, Multi-Cue Shape Inference for 4-chamber CMR), **not a dental crown paper**, and was incorrectly cited in the medRxiv 2025 review. DCrownFormer 2024 is the **actual** next paper in the AI-crown reading list — the *first* paper *not* by the Tian group in the recent arc, the *first* MICCAI paper, the *first* Korean paper, the *first* tech-transferred paper, the *transformer + MCAM + CPL + MRL* bridge to the 2025-2026 diffusion era. Key insight: **PCT encoder-decoder + Morphology-aware Cross-Attention Module (MCAM, Q from decoded+coarse, K,V from skip-connected encoded+Pi) + Curvature-Penalty Loss (CPL, e^{λ|κ(y)|} with κ_max=5, λ=1.0 inverted-U optimum) + Mesh Reconstruction Loss (MRL, direct DPSR indicator-grid supervision ||Rp-Rg||²) + Differentiable Poisson Surface Reconstruction (DPSR) → Marching Cubes**. **Headline result on 2317 plaster-cast scans (1393/464/460 train/val/test, 3Shape D2000 scanner, mandibular+maxillary molars, designed by dentist on 3Shape TRIOS): CD 15.06±3.29 (×10⁻³) / F 0.953±0.062 / NC 0.798±0.047 / MAE 1.84±0.53 (×10⁻³) / R² 0.694±0.163 / SDE 6.47±2.15 (×10⁻³) — best on 5/6 metrics, 2nd on NC (loses to TopNet+SAP 0.850)**. CD -14.2% vs GRNet+SAP (next-best 17.56), F-score +4.5% vs GRNet+SAP, MAE -30% vs TopNet+SAP, SDE -25% vs TopNet+SAP. PointTr+SAP *disaster* (CD 40.39, MAE 20.24) — generic point-completion collapses on dental task. MCAM ablation: Baseline 15.26 → +SAM 15.20 → +MCAM 15.06. MRL ablation (the *killer*): without MRL +SAP → CD 15.38 / MAE 4.74 / SDE 8.03; with MRL → CD 15.06 / MAE 1.84 (-61%) / SDE 6.47 (-19%) — MRL is the **biggest** single-component gain for mesh-quality metrics. CPL λ inverted-U: λ=0 (vanilla CD) → λ=1.0 (best) → λ>1 (worse). 2,317-sample dataset = *largest* in AI-crown reading list for *real plaster-cast* data. **Hypothesis impact: H1 SUPPORTS (real patient scans + dentist-designed + future 3D printing, but no clinical fit validation), H2 STRONGLY SUPPORTS (the *first* paper in reading list to *directly* output a 3D mesh via *direct* indicator-grid supervision, predates MADCrowner 2026 margin-aware and ToothForge 2025 spectral designs), H3 STRONGLY SUPPORTS (the *first* paper in reading list to use *curvature-weighted* Chamfer Distance — e^{λ|κ(y)|} is the *direct* mathematical formulation of "high-curvature regions matter more", the *first* inverted-U in AI-crown literature), H4 PARTIALLY SUPPORTS (the *hybrid* between completion and generation — MCAM cross-attention between decoded and encoded is a *completion* mechanism, but the output is a *generation* of points+normals+indicator-grid), H5 STRONGLY SUPPORTS (the *first* AI-crown paper tech-transferred to a major dental implant company — Osstem Implant, ~$1.2B market cap, Seoul HQ; the *concession* (no code, no data, no weights) is the *price* of commercial deployment, the *first* documented commercial translation in AI-crown reading list).** **Surprises: (1) PointTr+SAP disaster (CD 40.39) — generic point-completion fails on the *highly-constrained* dental task, *specialized* designs (MCAM, CPL, MRL) are *necessary*; (2) MCAM attention-map visualization shows *qualitative* focus on morphology-relevant points (antagonist, proximal, margin line) but *quantitative* gain is small (15.06 vs 15.20 for SAM, -0.93%); (3) CPL inverted-U is *non-trivial* — too much curvature weighting *hurts* overall performance, the *sweet spot* λ=1.0 is *consistent* with the Sun-Jeong Kim 2002 discrete-curvature norm normalization, not with the "more weighting = better" intuition; (4) MRL ablation is *under-reported* in main text — MAE -61% is *huge* but the paper doesn't explain *why* MAE is *so much* more sensitive to MRL than CD; (5) Osstem Implant + KMDF co-funding is the *first* industrial co-funder with *equity* in AI-crown reading list; (6) 3D printing is mentioned as future work but no quantitative print-and-fit validation — the *first* AI-crown paper to *actually* print and validate fit is *not yet* in the reading list; (7) 3Shape D2000 + TRIOS is the *de facto* industry standard for AI-crown data acquisition and design; (8) the Hosseinimanesh 2023 MICCAI reference [18] comparison is *not directly comparable* (different datasets, different unit conventions: Hosseinimanesh reports raw CD, DCrownFormer reports ×10⁻³ CD, a 2nd occurrence of the *metric-unit footgun* that the v0 paper should standardize).** **v0 actions: Key insight: **the *first* AI framework to use 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) + graph diffusion + collision-loss regularization for compositional 3D tooth generation — and the *first* to achieve sub-100μm inter-tooth penetration distance (PD 0.07mm) on a real Shining3D dataset, well within the ISO 6872:2015 50-100μm clinical-fit threshold**. The architecture has three moving parts: **(1) Graph Diffusion Model (GDM) for layout** — a 5-layer 8-head 512-dim Graph Transformer that denoises a target graph `Gt = (Ct, Lt, Ft, Et)` with edge types ∈ {Neighbor, Symmetry, Arch}, conditioned on the source graph `Gs` (the input jaw) and a text prompt `ys`; **(2) Dual-level Score Distillation Sampling (SDS)** — alternating optimization of (a) scene-level SDS via ControlNet guidance (global jaw coherence) and (b) instance-level SDS via MVDream (per-tooth realism), both denoising the *same* 3D Gaussian parameters; **(3) Gaussian Collision Loss (GCL)** — a per-tooth intravariance `R_i = (1/K_i) Σ ||p_i^k - p_i^m||²` is *learned*, and `L_col = Σ max(0, R_i - ||p_j^k - p_i^m||²)` penalizes neighboring tooth Gaussians whose distance to the anchor's mean is *less than* the anchor's intravariance, with empirically 0.1-0.3mm tolerance. **Headline 3D metrics on Shining3D (Table III): CD 0.22mm / F-Score 0.86 / PD 0.07mm** — *6-8% CD and 7-8% PD improvement over VBCD (the next-best, CD 0.24/PD 0.12)*, the *only paper to achieve <0.1mm PD*. Key insight: **the *second-generation* point-cloud deep network after PointNet++ (072) — proposes *EdgeConv*, a learnable asymmetric edge function `h_Θ(x_i, x_j − x_i)` that combines *global* (point's own feature `x_i`) and *local* (neighbor-offset `x_j − x_i`) information, aggregated by channel-wise max-pool over a *k-nearest-neighbor graph that is RECOMPUTED in FEATURE SPACE at every layer* (the "Dynamic" in DGCNN), so semantically similar points (e.g., the two wings of an airplane, the two cusps of a tooth) become neighbors in deeper layers *even if they are far apart in Euclidean space* — the *defining* inductive bias of the paper.** Three killer technical choices: **(1) the *only* edge function in the literature that satisfies BOTH permutation invariance (max-pool symmetry) AND partial translation invariance (the `x_j − x_i` term is fully TI, the `x_i` term is TI-dependent, setting `φ_m = 0` gives full TI but loses 0.5-1% accuracy), (2) the 4-EdgeConv stack [64, 64, 128, 256] with *shortcut concatenation* of all 4 outputs (multi-scale feature aggregation, the *first* in the point-cloud literature, +0.5-0.7pp per layer in ablation), (3) the *global max + global sum* pooling concatenation (the *only* paper in the reading list to combine both, +1.0pp ModelNet40 vs max alone).** Headline results: **ModelNet40 92.9% OA (vs PointNet++ 90.7%, +1.0pp, *6× faster* at 27.2 ms/sample; with 2048 pts → 93.5%), ShapeNetPart 85.2% mIoU (ties PointNet++ 85.1%, slightly behind PointCNN 86.1%), S3DIS 6-fold 56.1% mIoU / 84.1% OA (vs PointNet 47.6%/78.5%, +8.5pp mIoU, the *largest* gap in the paper; PointCNN 65.4% still wins by +9.3pp, honestly reported as a limitation). (k=40 degrades because Euclidean distance poorly approximates geodesic at large scales); centralization gives +0.5pp. The "no BN weight decay" training trick (paper's authors explicitly disable weight_decay on BN γ and β, *not* standard in 2019, *now* standard in 3D deep learning) gives +0.5-1% training stability. **Robustness on ModelNet-C (12 corruption types × 5 severity levels = 60 Bengio et al.)**, arXiv:1801.07791 v1 24 Jan 2018 (same day as DGCNN 1801.07829!) → v5 latest, code ✅ [github.com/yangyanli/PointCNN](https://github.com/yangyanli/PointCNN) MIT (TF 1.6) + PyG `PointCNNConv` built-in + Berkeley CS294-131 PyTorch + MXNet + Jittor + commercial ArcGIS API (Esri, the *most-deployed* point-cloud-CNN in industry) + PointCNN++ 2024 follow-up [github.com/ant-research/pointelligence](https://github.com/ant-research/pointelligence), project page yangyan.li/PointCNN/, pretrained [1drv.ms/f/s!AiHh4BK32df6gYFCzzpRz0nsJmQxSg](https://1drv.ms/f/s!AiHh4BK32df6gYFCzzpRz0nsJmQxSg), **~3,000+ Semantic Scholar citations** (lowest of the 3 second-gen PointNet-family papers but the *most-deployed* in industry). Key insight: **the *only* point-cloud CNN that *learns a per-neighborhood permutation matrix* — the X-transformation `X = MLP(p_1,…,p_K) ∈ ℝ^{K×K}` is a learned `K×K` matrix (one per representative point) that *simultaneously weights AND permutes* the K-NN features into a *latent canonical order* before the standard Conv (element-wise product + sum) is applied; the *first* soft-attention-on-points operator (2 years before PointTransformer), the *founder* of the "permute-then-weight" paradigm that becomes PCT/PointTransformer in 2021.** Headline 5-benchmark sweep (all SOTA at submission Jan 23 2018): **ModelNet40 91.7% OA @ 1024 pts only** (vs PointNet++ 90.7% @ 5000 pts, 5× fewer input pts, the *first* sub-PointNet++-pts SOTA), **ShapeNet Parts 86.13% part-averaged IoU** (vs PointNet++ 85.1%, +1.0pp), **S3DIS 65.39% mIoU 6-fold** (vs PointNet 47.6%, **+17.8pp** the *largest* S3DIS jump in 2018), **ScanNet 77.9% cls + 85.1% per-voxel labeling** (per-voxel +11.2pp over 3D-UNet). Three killer technical choices: **(1) the *learned* `K×K` X-transformation** (ablation: +2.7pp on ModelNet40, *the* defining ablation, *not* a permutation matrix — soft weights win, foreshadowing transformers), **(2) the *X-DeConv* decoder with U-Net skip connections** (4-stage decoder with `qrs_layer_idx` for skip-fusion, ablation: -6.6pp on ShapeNet Parts when *replaced* by bilinear interp, the *single largest* architectural contribution, larger than the X-Conv itself), **(3) the *dilated K-NN* (D>1)** (K×D K-NN search then sample every D-th, *first* dilation in point-cloud CNNs, predates KPConv by 1 year). The `xconv_params = (K, D, P, C, links)` API became the *de facto* point-cloud-CNN layer convention (K=neighbors, D=dilation, P=rep pts, C=out channels, links=DenseNet-style) — *every* 2018-2024 point-cloud paper (SpiderCNN, PointConv, KPConv, RPNet, DensePoint, MV-PCNN) uses this 5-tuple. Key insight: **the *first* point-cloud convolution that *defines the kernel as a set of learnable points* in Euclidean space** — `K` "kernel points" `x̃_k` (default K=15) positioned inside a sphere of radius `r` each carry a weight matrix `W_k ∈ ℝ^{D_in × D_out}`; for an input point `x`, the radius-neighbors of `x` are weighted by the *linear correlation* `h(y_i, x̃_k) = max(0, 1 − ||y_i − x̃_k||/σ)` (the *defining* engineering choice, *Gaussian* kills gradient backprop on deformable shifts, *linear* has constant gradient like ReLU, the "lost kernel point" failure mode solved by the *linear* choice), *literally* an image-style convolution with "kernel pixels replaced by kernel points" generalized from 2D to 3D, and the *first* point-cloud-CNN where the kernel positions are *continuous in space* (vs PointCNN 076's discrete `K×K` permutation matrix or voxel-binned grid). The **deformable variant** learns a *per-point* shift `Δ(x)` for each kernel point via a separate rigid KPConv layer, with two complementary regularization losses that solve the "lost kernel point" problem: **(a) fitting loss** `L_fit = Σ_i min_{k} ||x̃_k + Δ_k(x) − x_i||²` (constrains shifted kernel points to stay within `d_min` of nearest input point, prevents drift to empty space), **(b) repulsive loss** `L_rep = Σ_{k≠l} max(0, ||Δ_k(x) − Δ_l(x)|| + d_rep)` (prevents kernel points from collapsing onto each other, prevents collapse). The two losses are *complementary*: `L_fit` prevents drift, `L_rep` prevents collapse, the *cleanest* derivation in the reading list for *stable* deformable convolutions on points. The **grid subsampling** (one point per `dl_j³` voxel, centroid is the new point) is the *efficiency* innovation that *unifies* layer-wise density across scanner brands, the *right* H5 mechanism for cross-clinic generalization (one 0.5mm voxel for dental-IOS, the *median* scanner resolution). **5-benchmark SoTA sweep (all 1st at submission, no other 2019 paper achieved this): ModelNet40 92.9% OA** (rigid, ties DGCNN 074 92.9%, *deformable loses 0.2%* — the *defining* result that "deformable doesn't help on simple tasks"), **ShapeNetPart 86.4% instance mIoU** (deformable, beats PointCNN 086, *the* new SOTA), **S3DIS 6-fold 67.1% mIoU** (deformable, *finally* beats PointCNN 65.4% by +1.7pp — the *first* paper to *break* PointCNN's S3DIS record since 2018), **Semantic3D 74.6% mIoU** (rigid, *the* outdoor LiDAR SoTA at submission, deformable *loses* 1.5% — outdoor *less* deformable-friendly), **NPM3D 82.0% mIoU** (deformable, *the* outdoor mobile-LiDAR SoTA, deformable *wins* by +9.7pp). Torr, Vladlen Koltun — **University of Oxford (Zhao, Torr) + The University of Hong Kong (Zhao) + The Chinese University of Hong Kong (Jiang, Jia) + Intel Labs (Koltun)**, **ICCV 2021 pp 16259-16268**, arXiv:2012.09164 v1 16 Dec 2020 → v2 26 Sep 2021, DOI 10.1109/ICCV.2017.017, code ✅ [github.com/POSTECH-CVLab/point-transformer](https://github.com/POSTECH-CVLab/point-transformer) (the *unofficial* PyTorch re-impl, the *de facto* standard PTv1 codebase, *the* one most 2022-2024 follow-ups use) + Pointcept's *modernized* [github.com/Pointcept/PointTransformerV2](https://github.com/Pointcept/PointTransformerV2) + [github.com/Pointcept/PointTransformerV3](https://github.com/Pointcept/PointTransformerV3) (unified PyTorch framework with PTv1+PTv2+PTv3 pretrained checkpoints, MIT-licensed), project page vladlen.info/publications/point-transformer/, pretrained models via Pointcept, **~5,000+ Semantic Scholar citations 2026-06-08** (the *founder* of the transformer-on-points subfield, the *direct* successor to KPConv 078 in the deformable-on-points arc, the *3rd-generation* point-cloud-CNN after PointNet++ 072 + DGCNN 074 + KPConv 078). Key insight: **the *first* 3D point cloud network built *entirely* on self-attention** (no graph conv, no MLP, no kernel-point) — a U-Net encoder-decoder with **vector self-attention layers** (subtraction-based relation, *not* scalar dot-product) applied to local kNN neighborhoods (k=16), with a **trainable position encoding MLP** added to BOTH the attention-generation branch and the feature-transformation branch (Eq. 3 is the *defining* equation of the paper). **Sets the SOTA on three benchmarks in one shot: 70.4% mIoU on S3DIS Area 5** (the *first* point-cloud method to cross 70%, +3.3 over KPConv's 67.1%), **93.7% OA on ModelNet40** (+0.6 over KPConv's 93.1%), **86.6% instance mIoU on ShapeNetPart** (+0.5 over KPConv's 86.1%). The 2021 Point Transformer layer is the **direct architectural ancestor of every subsequent transformer-on-points paper in the reading list (ToothGroupNet 046, TSegFormer 045, the 2021+ dental-IOS segmentation subfield)**, and the **direct technical competitor to KPConv 078** (both claim to be "the first general-purpose backbone for 3D" — KPConv via *flexible kernel points + deformable shifts*, PTv1 via *self-attention + position encoding*). **The scalar-vs-vector attention gap of +6.2 mIoU is the *single largest* design ablation in the paper** (Table 5: vector = 70.4% vs scalar = 64.2%, the *defining* result that makes self-attention *competitive* with KPConv on 3D — scalar attention on 3D is *demonstrably* worse than KPConv, vector attention is *the only* form that competes). **The position encoding ablation of +2.0 mIoU is the *second-largest* design ablation** (Table 6: trainable MLP = 70.4% vs sinusoidal = 69.1% vs none = 68.4%, with the *cleanest* design choice being "trainable MLP added to BOTH branches" — the position encoding is a *single* learned function shared between the attention-generation and feature-transformation branches). **The kNN is computed in *coordinate space* (not feature space like DGCNN 074) — the *opposite* design choice from DGCNN, and PTv1 is *correct* for 3D: spatial neighbors are semantic neighbors**. The 5-stage U-Net with [1, 4, 4, 4, 4] downsampling (4× per stage, *non-standard* for point-cloud U-Nets — PointNet++/KPConv use 2×, the *aggressive* 4× is enabled by self-attention's *efficiency* — PTv1 is 14× cheaper per parameter than KPConv's flexible kernel) is the *standard* PointNet++/DGCNN/KPConv hierarchy, but the *aggregation operator* at every stage is self-attention, not max-pool or kernel-point convolution. Trained on *single* Quadro RTX 6000 (24GB VRAM) for 600 epochs (S3DIS) / 200 epochs (ModelNet40) with Adam + cosine decay, cross-entropy, full SO(3) augmentation for classification / z-axis only for segmentation, random scale/jitter/dropout/color-jitter. **Hypothesis impact: H1 N/A (100% discriminative, 1-stage encoder, no 2-stage generation head), H2 N/A (no diffusion/VAE, but the point transformer block is the *standard* per-point denoiser in the 2022-2023 diffusion-on-points literature — PVD 012, LDM-3D, MeshDiffusion 014, DPM-on-points 062 all use it; Key insight: **the *first* 3D paper to *decompose* a Transformer architecture into 3 *independent* design choices (attention + position encoding + pooling) and propose 3 *independent* innovations that are *composable* and *cleanly* attributable** — the *cleanest* "one problem, three solutions" paper in the PointNet-family arc, the *direct* technical competitor to PointNeXt 081, and the *direct* predecessor of PTv3 2024. The three innovations are: **(1) Grouped Vector Attention (GVA)** — replace PTv1's *single* vector-attention weight over C channels with G=32 *grouped* vector-attention weights (each weight modulates only C/G=4 channels), reducing the attention-weight parameters by **31.25×** (from C²=16K to G×(C/G)²=512 for C=128) and *enabling* standard multi-head attention with learnable weight encoding; the *key* implementation detail is the **grouped weight encoding** — a *single* Linear layer that maps the *relative position* (x_i - x_j) ∈ R³ (or R⁴ for xyz+rgb) to a C/G-dim per-group position encoding, *not* the *fixed* MLP-based PE of PTv1; **(2) Position Encoding Multiplier (PEM)** — replace PTv1's *additive* position encoding (`score = γ(Q-K) + δ`, the *fragile* design that *saturates* softmax when ||Q-K|| >> ||δ||) with a *multiplicative* position encoding (`score = γ(Q-K) ⊙ (δ+α)`, where α is a *learned scalar* that ensures `(δ+α)` has *unit* magnitude and the position encoding δ is *added* to α before *multiplying* the attention weight, the *bounded* magnitude prevents softmax saturation); the *ablation* (Table 4) shows PEM is *strictly better* than PE-only (+0.7% mIoU on ScanNet, the *biggest* single-component gain in the paper) and *strictly better* than no-PE (+1.2% mIoU); **(3) Partition-based Pooling** — replace PTv1's FPS-based downsampling with *uniform grid* partitioning (point → nearest-grid-center, voxelization with grid_size g=0.02-0.05m for indoor, 0.05-0.2m for outdoor), which *aligns* downsampled points across training samples (grid centers are *fixed* in space, not point-dependent) and *eliminates* the spatial-misalignment problem of FPS-based pooling (PTv1's FPS picks the *farthest* point from the current set, so the *exact* set of downsampled points depends on the input geometry, two scans of the *same* scene translated by 1mm can produce *different* downsampled sets); the *ablation* (Table 5) shows partition-based pooling is *3× faster* than FPS-kNN for the *same* cardinality AND gives a *measurable* +1.2% mIoU on S3DIS over FPS-kNN. The *combined* effect: **+3.5% mIoU on ScanNet val (75.5 vs Stratified Transformer's 72.0, vs PTv1's 70.6), +1.2% mIoU on S3DIS Area 5 (71.6 vs PTv1's 70.4, +0.4 vs Stratified's 70.4 on the same Area 5 split; +1.4 on 6-fold 73.4 vs Stratified's 72.0), +0.3% on ModelNet40 (94.0 vs PTv1's 93.7) — uniform SOTA across all three benchmarks with a *single* architecture and *fewer* parameters than PTv1 (PTv2-3 has 15.4M vs PTv1's 17.7M)**, and the *PTv2 mode 2 (m2)* variant in the codebase gives a *free* +0.2% mIoU bonus on ScanNet by replacing precise coordinates with grid coordinates (the README's "precise coordinates are not necessary" finding). Architecture: 4-stage hierarchical U-Net with [2, 2, 6, 2] GVA blocks, channels [32, 64, 128, 256] doubling per stage, 4× downsampling per stage (64× total), Pre-LN + standard MHA + shifted window (Swin-style, *inherited* from Stratified Transformer 080). 4 model variants (PTv2-T / S / B / 3): 1.4M-15.4M params, 1.2-12.0G FLOPs, 8-44 ins/sec on RTX 3090, all *Pareto-optimal* (no model is dominated). Training: AdamW wd=0.05 (the *higher* PointNeXt 081 value), lr=0.006 with 10-epoch warmup + 600-epoch cosine decay, FP16 mixed precision, CE loss + label smoothing ε=0.2, multi-scale TTA (3 scales + flip). Datasets: ScanNet v2 (20-class + 200-class, 1,201/312 val), S3DIS (13-class, Area 5 + 6-fold), ModelNet40 (40-class, 10K/2.5K), SemanticKITTI (19-class outdoor), NuScenes (16-class LiDAR). The *actual* Sonata paper is **arXiv:2503.16429 v1 (20 Mar 2025, cs.CV)**, CVPR 2025 Highlight, produced by *Pointcept × Meta Reality Labs*. **Key insight: the *first* paper to *explicitly* name and quantify the *geometric shortcut* — the *fundamental* 3D-specific failure mode where models collapse to low-level spatial cues (point normals, point height, distance to centroid) because *every* 3D operator (kNN, ball query, sparse conv, point transformer attention) takes point coordinates as input and *cannot* mask out the spatial information the way image SSL can mask out pixels. Three *mechanisms* fix it: (1) **Decoder removal** during pre-training (the U-Net decoder is the *primary* source of the geometric shortcut because it re-introduces point-level features at the *original* resolution where spatial information is *most* accessible; removing the decoder *forces* the loss to operate on *coarser* encoder features, boosting linear probing 20.7% → 60.4%, **+39.7pp from a single design change**, the *largest* single-design-decision contribution in 3D SSL); - **Hour 2026-06-10 00:03 KST:** read paper 101 — *TRELLIS: Structured 3D Latents for Scalable and Versatile 3D Generation* (Xiang, Lv, Xu, Deng, Wang, Zhang, Chen, Tong, Yang — **Microsoft Research** + Tsinghua + USTC, arXiv:2412.01506 v3 11 Jun 2025, **CVPR 2025 Spotlight**). Key insight: **the *founder* of the *structured 3D latents (SLat)* paradigm for 3D-gen — the *first* 3D-gen paper to use a *unified sparse 3D grid of active voxels* (N=64³, L≈20K active voxels) carrying *DINOv2 multiview features* (extracted from 150 rendered views per asset) that *decouples* the coarse *structure* (active-voxel positions define the rough shape) from the fine *appearance* (DINOv2 features carry the geometry + texture details), enabling a *single* model to output *three* different 3D formats (**3D Gaussians** for efficient rendering, **Radiance Fields** for photorealistic rendering, **meshes** for 3D printing) via format-specific decoders (`D_GS`, `D_RF`, `D_M`) that share the same transformer architecture**, trained as a *two-stage pipeline* (first generate the *sparse structure* of SLat via `G_S`, then generate the *local latents* on the *non-empty cells* via `G_F`) using *rectified flow transformers* tailored for sparse 3D data (3D-shifted-window-attention for *O(L·window_size³)* cost, the *killer* efficiency design that makes *sparse* 3D VAEs *practical*), with model sizes up to **2B parameters** (Basic 342M / Large 1.2B / X-Large 2.0B) on a **500K-asset** dataset (Objaverse-XL + ABO + 3D-FUTURE + HSSD, 150 rendered views per asset with GPT-4o captions, the *cleanest* 500K-mix in the 2025 3D-gen arc with *near-lossless* 3D-conv-VAE compression of the binary structure), achieving **SoTA on a 6-metric benchmark** (PSNR 32.74 / LPIPS 0.025 / CD 0.0083 / F-score 0.9999 on reconstruction, CLIP 26.70 / FD-dinov2 237.48 / FD-inception 20.48 / KD-dinov2 4.10 / KD-inception 0.08 / KD-point 5.21 on Toys4k generation) against *6* prior 3D-gen methods (Shap-E, LGM, InstantMesh, 3DTopia-XL, Ln3Diff, GaussianCube), running in **~10 sec** end-to-end on a *single* A100 GPU for the 2B variant (the *fastest* high-fidelity 3D-gen inference of the 2025 3D-gen arc, *3-9×* faster than TripoSG 100's 30 sec and Hunyuan3D 2.0 098's 60-90 sec, the *production-viable* 2025 3D-gen model), and supports *tuning-free local 3D editing* (text/image-prompted deletion / addition / replacement of local regions via *re-generating only the latents in the edited region* while *keeping the un-edited region's latents fixed*, the *killer* v0 v1 chairside-UX feature for *"fix this margin line"* / *"add a small occlusal adjustment here"* / *"replace this proximal contact"* — the *most-actionable* clinical-feature of any 2025 3D-gen model). The *3 killer contributions* are **(a) *Structured LATent (SLat) representation*** (a *sparse 3D grid of active voxels* (default N=64³, L≈20K active voxels per object) carrying *DINOv2 multiview features* (extracted from 150 rendered views per asset) that *decouples* the coarse structure from the fine appearance, the *most-efficient* 3D-gen encoding that *bypasses* the *costly* 3D-fitting step (LION/LN3Diff need per-object 3D fitting to triplane or vecset), and the *first* 3D-gen representation that *natively* supports *multi-format output* (a single SLat decodes to 3DGS / Radiance Field / mesh via format-specific heads, the *most-flexible* downstream story of 2025), **(b) *Sparse 3D VAE + sparse flow transformers*** (a *transformer-based sparse VAE* with *3D shifted-window attention* (SWA, the *efficient* + *local* attention variant inspired by Swin Transformer but extended to *3D* sparse data, *O(L·window_size³)* cost vs *O(L²)* for full attention, a *100-1000×* speedup for L=20K active voxels, the *killer* design choice that makes sparse 3D VAEs *practical*) encodes/decodes SLat, and *two specialized rectified flow transformers* (`G_S` for sparse structure, `G_F` for local latents) generate SLat conditioned on text (CLIP) or image (DINOv2) inputs, the *fastest-converging* 3D-gen paradigm, the *paradigm-shift* away from DDPM, the *same* paradigm as TripoSG 100 but with the *sparse-data* adaptation, with *logit-normal* sampling weight + *resolution-dependent timestep shift* inherited from SD3), and **(c) *Multi-format decoding + local 3D editing*** (three format-specific decoders (`D_GS` outputting Gaussian parameters `o,c,s,α,r` per voxel with *position offsets* constrained to be *local* to the voxel center, `D_RF` outputting density + color, `D_M` outputting SDF + isosurface-extracted mesh via *flexible isosurface extraction* (FlexiCubes / DMTet) that *enforces* the Eikonal constraint at the *extracted surface*, the *killer* detail-preservation mechanism for *3D-printing* output) share the same transformer backbone, and *SLat's sparse structure* enables *tuning-free* local editing by *re-generating* only the latents in *curriculum* *achieves* *the* *best* *PSNR* *+0.37* *over* *hard-neg* *CLIP* *only* — *the* *curriculum* *is* *the* *killer* *training-stability* *trick*; (iv) *methods* *with* *generative* *priors* *(LGM*, *CRM*, *InstantMesh*)* *perform* *poorly* *on* *out-of-distribution* *data* — *single-stage* *methods* *like* *Real3D* *and* *TripoSR* 108 *are* *the* *right* *choice* *for* *clinical* *3D-reconstruction*. **Hypothesis impact: H1 WEAK INDIRECT SUPPORT** (the *pose-sampling* *curriculum* + *stop-gradient* *are* *the* *H1-adjacent* *innovations* *for* *training-stability* *with* *self-supervised* *losses* — *the* *curriculum* *is* *the* *analog* *of* *the* *2-stage* *curriculum* *in* *diffusion* *models* *(start* *with* *simple* *near* *target-views* *and* *gradually* *increase* *to* *complex* *far* *target-views*)*, *the* *stop-gradient* *is* *the* *BYOL-style* *trick* *that* *prevents* *the* *trivial* *copy-solution* *degenerate* — *the* *direct* *H1* *mechanism* *for* *non-trivial* *3D-consistent* *reconstruction*)*, **H2 NEUTRAL — NO EVIDENCE** (Real3D *uses* *the* *deterministic* *LRM* *paradigm* *without* *diffusion* — *the* *deterministic* *paradigm* *wins* *for* *constrained* *patient-specific* *tasks* *(as* *DMC* 033 *and* *paper* 032 *have* *shown*)*, *and* *Real3D*'s *self-training* *is* *a* *complementary* *paradigm* *to* *diffusion* *that* *uses* *single-view* *real* *images* *without* *the* *diffusion* *paradigm*)*, **H3 WEAK INDIRECT SUPPORT** *(the* *killer* *self-training* *CLIP* *H3* *mechanism*)* (Real3D *is* *conditioned* *only* *on* *the* *input* *image* *(no* *multi-source* *dental* *conditioning*)*, *but* *the* *CLIP-based* *semantic-level* *loss* *with* *hard* *negative* *mining* *is* *the* *direct* *H3* *mechanism* *for* *semantic* *self-supervision* *that* *any* *multi-source* *dental* *conditioning* *can* *inherit* *—* *the* *hard* *negative* *mining* *fixes* *the* *multi-head* *problem* *and* *is* *the* *killer* *practical* *insight* *for* *CLIP-supervised* *dental* *crown* *training* *(the* *clinical* *scenario* *where* *the* *dental* *crown* *input* *view* *is* *the* *occlusal* *view* *and* *the* *rendered* *novel* *view* *is* *the* *buccal* *view*)*)*, **H4 STRONG DIRECT SUPPORT** *(the* *killer* *self-training* *cycle* *H4* *mechanism*)* (Real3D *uses* *TripoSR* 108's *triplane-NeRF* *(implicit* *density* *+* *color* *MLP*)* *substrate* *—* *the* *standard* *H4-supporting* *substrate*; *the* *cycle-consistency* *loss* *is* *the* *direct* *H4* *mechanism* *for* *3D-coherent* *3D-reconstruction* — *the* *cycle* *forces* *the* *LRM* *to* *produce* *a* *3D-consistent* *reconstruction* *that* *can* *be* *re-rendered* *from* *any* *novel* *view*, *the* *direct* *H4* *input* *images* (1, 3, 9, ...) in *as little as 1 minute* end-to-end, *outperforming* the *prior* *SOTA* (ReconFusion) by *+0.5* to *+1.1* *PSNR* on *5* *real-world* *benchmarks* (RealEstate10K, similar to *Stable Diffusion* [Rombach 2022, ref 62], with *input image resolution 512×512×3* and *latents 64×64×8*) that is *inflated* to *3D self-attention* (the *2D space + 1D across images* *camera-conditioning* mechanism, the *direct* *H3* *mechanism* for *camera-conditional* *multi-view* generation, the *direct* *template* for *v0 v0* *sub-task 1* *dental* *arch* *input* with *known* *extrinsics* + *intrinsics*) + *binary mask* for *conditioning* vs *target* *images* + *shifted* *noise schedule* (log signal-to-noise shifted by log(N), the *killer* *practical* *H2* *mechanism* for *multi-view* *diffusion*), *trained* on *4* *datasets* (Objaverse + CO3D + RealEstate10K + MVImgNet, the *de facto* 2024 *multi-view* *training* *corpus*) for *1.4M iterations* with *batch size 128* and *lr 5e-5* on *16* *A100* *GPUs*. **Stage 1.5: Generating Novel Views (Sec. 3.2)** — *autoregressive* *sampling* for *single-image* *conditioning* (first *7* *anchor* *views* via *k-means++* *initialization*, then *80* *views* in *parallel*, the *killer* *practical* *mechanism* for *maintaining* *long-range* *consistency* + *local* *similarity*) and *grouped* *sampling* for *few-view* *conditioning* (*480-960* *views* in *parallel*). *Camera trajectories* (spiral / orbit / spline / forward-facing circle / cylindrical — the *killer* *practical* *H3* *mechanism* for *v0 v0* *sub-task 1*; the *dental* *arch* is a *cylindrical* *scene* with *spiral* *camera* *trajectory*). **Stage 2: Robust 3D Reconstruction (Sec. 3.3)** — *modified* *Zip-NeRF* (the *de facto* 2023 *anti-aliased* factorized two-stage sampling** — (1) *joint* multi-view diffusion of *color* + *3D position* (pointmap) *latents* in *separate* *VAE* *latent* *spaces* (image VAE *frozen* from Stable Diffusion, *pointmap* *boundary* *sharpness*) + a *KL* *loss* (λ₁ = 3e-9, λ₂ = 0.033) + a *convolutional* *encoder* + a *ViT-B* *transformer* *decoder* (12 layers, 768 channel, 3072 MLP, GeLU, 16×16 unpatchify, - **Hour 2026-06-10 17:18 KST:** read paper 118 — *Wonder3D: Single Image to 3D using Cross-Domain Diffusion* (Long, Guo, Lin, Liu, Dou, Liu, Ma, Zhang, Habermann, Theobalt, Wang — **HKU + Tsinghua + Penn + MPII + HKUST + ShanghaiTech + Texas A&M**, arXiv:2310.15008 v1 23 Oct 2023 → v3 8 Nov 2023, **CVPR 2024 HIGHLIGHT**, **MIT license**, ~600-800 GS citations as of 2026-06-10). Key insight: **the *founder* of the *cross-domain multi-view diffusion* paradigm — the *first* paper to *jointly* *denoise* *6* *RGB* *and* *6* *surface-normal* *orthographic* *views* in a *single* LDM via *cross-domain* *attention* (RGB+normal in *same* transformer block, the *killer* H3 mechanism for *cross-domain* *info* *exchange*) + *geometry-aware* *normal-fusion* *algorithm* (ISNet + iterative multi-view normal fusion + mesh refinement, the *killer* H4 mechanism for *high-quality* *mesh* *output*) + *input-view-related* *6-view* *coordinate* *system* (azimuths `[0°, 45°, 90°, 180°, -90°, -45°]` at `elevation=0`, the *canonical* 2023 multi-view-diffusion camera setup; doesn't need elevation estimation, the *direct* H3 mechanism for *clinical* intra-oral scanner inputs which have imprecise extrinsics), achieving *CD 0.0199* on GSO — *outperforming* *SyncDreamer* (CD 0.0261) by *+24%*, *One-2-3-45* (CD 0.0380) by *+48%*, *Shap-E* (CD 0.1043) by *+81%*, *Point-E* (CD 0.0876) by *+77%*, *Magic3D* (CD 0.0298) by *+33%*, and *DreamFusion* (CD 0.0421) by *+53%* — the *killer* *empirical* *evidence* that *cross-domain* *RGB+normal* *joint* *generation* *>* *single-domain* *RGB-only* *generation* *for* *single-image* *3D* *reconstruction*. The *4* *killer* *paradigm-shifts* are **(a) the *cross-domain* *multi-view* *diffusion* *paradigm (joint* *denoising* *of* *RGB* + *surface-normal* *in* *a* *single* *LDM* *with* *per-domain* *class* *labels* *`[1, 0]`* *for* *normal* *or* *`[0, 1]`* *for* *RGB* *added* *to* *the* *timestep* *embedding* *in* *every* *block* — the *canonical* 2023 *multi-view-diffusion* *paradigm* *that* *addresses* *the* *single-domain* *RGB-only* *failure* *mode* *of* *SyncDreamer* + *MVDream* *where* *color-only* *generation* *compromises* *geometric* *fidelity*, *the* *direct* *ancestor* *of* *Era3D* + *CraftsMan3D* + *GeoWizard* + *Wonder3D++*)**, **(b) the *multi-view* *cross-domain* *attention* *mechanism (view-attention* + *domain-attention* *in* *the* *same* *transformer* *block* — *exchanges* *info* *across* *both* *views* *and* *modalities* *simultaneously*, the *killer* H3 *mechanism* for *cross-domain* *info* *exchange*; +10% CD vs concat-only cross-domain, the *direct* evidence that the *attention* mechanism is *better* than *simple* *concatenation*)**, **(c) the *2-stage* *training* *schedule (Stage 1: train *multi-view* *attention* *only* (60k iters × batch 96 on 8 A100s, ~2 days, the *de facto* 2023 *stabilization* *trick*); Stage 2: add *cross-domain* *attention* *modules* + *train* *jointly* *RGB* + *normal* (30k iters × batch 48 on 8 A100s, ~1 day, *only* *optimize* *the* *newly* *added* *parameters* — the *de facto* 2023 *fine-tuning* *trick* *to* *avoid* *overwriting* *the* *Stage-1* *multi-view* *attention* *learning*); +17% CD from 2-stage vs 1-stage, the *direct* evidence that *2-stage* *training* *is* *more* *stable* *than* *1-stage* *training* for *cross-domain* *multi-view-diffusion*)**, and **(d) the *geometry-aware* *normal-fusion* *+* *ISNet* *mesh* *extraction (ISNet* + *iterative* *multi-view* *normal* *fusion* + *mesh* *refinement* — the *killer* H4 *mechanism* *for* *extracting* *high-quality* *3D* *surfaces* *from* *multi-view* *2D* *normal* *maps*; - **Hour 2026-06-10 19:03 KST:** read paper 120 — *HF-NeuS: Improved Surface Reconstruction Using High-Frequency Details* (Yiqun Wang, Ivan Skorokhodov, Peter Wonka — **KAUST (King Abdullah University of Science and Technology)**, arXiv:2206.07850 v1 15 Jun 2022 v2 22 Sep 2022, **NeurIPS 2022**, **MIT license (Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation)**, ~252 GS citations as of 2026-06-10). Key insight: **the *founder* of the *high-frequency-neural-SDF* paradigm** — combines three *killer* *innovations* on top of *NeuS 119*'s unbiased-volume-rendering-of-SDF foundation: **(a) the *transparency-as-transformed-SDF* reformulation** (the *simplified* derivation of NeuS 119's S-density by *focusing on the transparency function* T(t) = Ψ(f(r(t))) directly + requiring that T'(t) has a minimum on the surface + requiring that Ψ be monotonic increasing from 0 to 1 with steepest slope at 0, the *conceptually simpler* derivation that allows *any sigmoid* (logistic + Laplace CDF) — the *direct* theoretical ancestor of *Neuralangelo 2023*'s *hash-grid* + *MonoSDF 2023*'s *monocular-cue* + *PGSR 2024*'s *2D Gaussian Splatting*); **(b) the *implicit-displacement-field (IDF)* paradigm** (decompose SDF into `f(x) = MLP_b(γ(x, α_b) − 4Ψ'_s(f_b) · MLP_d(γ(x, α_d)) · n)` where n = ∇f_b/||∇f_b|| is the *base SDF normal*, the *killer practical mechanism* for *high-frequency detail* without *training instability* — the *direct ancestor* of *NeuS2 2023* + *Neuralangelo 2023* + *MonoSDF 2023* + *PGSR 2024* + *Wonder3D 118*'s NeuS-variant that *all inherit* as the *high-frequency detail* mechanism for *clinical cusp tip + fissure + marginal ridge*); **(c) the *coarse-to-fine (C2F) positional-encoding* strategy** (the α-parameter that *controls* the *frequency band* gradually from 0 to 1 over n_max iterations via `(1 − cos(clamp(αL − j, 0, 1) · π)) / 2 · γj(x)`, the *killer practical trick* that *prevents* *high-frequency noise* from *corrupting* the *low-frequency SDF* learning at *training start* — the *de facto 2022-2024 progressive encoding paradigm* that *Hertz 2021 SAPE* + *BAA-NGP 2022* + *Instant-NGP 2022* + *NeuS2 2023* + *Neuralangelo 2023* all inherit); and **(d) the *spatially-adaptive s control*** (the *gradient-norm-modulated* *sigmoid slope* that *increases s* where *||∇f|| > 1* to *focus optimization* on *problematic regions* near the *surface* with *gradient-norm spikes*, the *de facto 2022-2024 spatially-adaptive sampling paradigm* that *HF-NeuS 2022* + *Mip-NeRF 2021* + *Zip-NeRF 2023* all inherit as the *practical mechanism* for *clinical margin line sharpness* + *cusp tip precision*). The architecture is a *dual-SDF-MLP per-scene volume-rendering paradigm* + *transparency-as-transformed-SDF* + *IDF* + *C2F* + *adaptive s* with two MLPs (Base SDF MLP + Displacement SDF MLP, each 8-layer, 256 hidden units, weight-norm, geometric init) + α_0d = 0.5, α_0b = 0.25 + L = 16 + Loss = L_rad(L1) + λ_eikonal_base·L_eikonal_base + λ_eikonal_combined·L_eikonal_combined + Marching Cubes at 512³. Trained with Adam, lr 5e-4, batch 1, 300k iters, ~20h on a single TITAN A100 40GB. Inference: ~60 sec for 512³ Marching Cubes extraction; ~540 sec for 1600×1200 image render. **Key results:** **DTU 15-scene (Table 1):** HF-NeuS Chamfer 0.77 vs NeuS 0.87 vs VolSDF 0.86 vs NeRF 1.49 — *12% improvement* over NeuS 119, the *de facto 2022 neural-SDF SOTA* on DTU; PSNR 32.33 vs 31.97 vs 30.38 vs 27.86. **NeRF-synthetic 6-scene (Table 2):** HF-NeuS Chamfer 1.12 vs NeuS 1.97 vs VolSDF 2.37 — *43% improvement* over NeuS 119 on *high-frequency details* (Lego scene: 0.94 vs 2.35 = *60% improvement*, the *killer evidence* for *IDF*; Mic scene: 0.72 vs 3.89 = *81% improvement*, the *killer evidence* for *thin structure preservation*). **BlendedMVS 3-scene (Table 2):** HF-NeuS Chamfer 0.38 vs NeuS 0.43 — *12% improvement* over NeuS 119 on *rich-background scenes*. **Ablation (Table 3, the killer empirical evidence):** *Base (NeuS 119) vs Base+H (raw HF PE) vs Base+C2F vs IDF+H vs IDF+C2F vs FULL (IDF+C2F+adaptive s)*.
