- **Hour 2026-06-10 20:10 KST:** read paper 121 — *Neuralangelo: High-Fidelity Neural Surface Reconstruction* (Zhaoshuo Li, Thomas Müller, Alex Evans, Russell H. Taylor, Mathias Unberath, Ming-Yu Liu, Chen-Hsuan Lin — **NVIDIA + Johns Hopkins**, arXiv:2306.03092 v1 5 Jun 2023 v2 13 Jun 2023, **CVPR 2023 Best Paper Honorable Mention**, **Apache 2.0 (code via NVIDIA Imaginaire)**, **~1,800-2,200 GS citations as of 2026-06-10**). Key insight: **the *founder* of the *hash-grid + neural-SDF + numerical-gradient + coarse-to-fine* paradigm — the *de facto 2023 production-grade neural surface reconstruction method*, 10× speedup over NeuS/HF-NeuS, scales to drone outdoor scenes without depth supervision.** Two killer innovations: **(a) the *numerical-gradient* trick for higher-order derivatives** (∇f(x) via finite differences: ∂f/∂x ≈ (f(x+ε) - f(x-ε))/(2ε), requires 6 additional SDF evaluations per query, but provides *non-local* information flow across hash cells — analytical gradient on hash-encoded features is *local* and backprop only updates local hash cells, causing noise artifacts; numerical gradient with ε larger than hash grid cell size = multiple cells contribute = non-local smoothing; the *killer* insight is that ε is *annealed* alongside the hash grid activation schedule, starting at the coarsest grid size and exponentially decreasing to the finest, giving coarse-to-fine smoothing), and **(b) the *coarse-to-fine hash-grid optimization* schedule** (only 4-8 coarsest levels active at start, progressively enable finer levels every 5000 iters as ε decreases; avoids "relearning" — finer grids don't need to undo what coarser grids learned; the canonical 2023 progressive-encoding paradigm that HF-NeuS 120's C2F predicted and the entire Instant-NGP ecosystem adopted). The loss is L = L_RGB + w_eik·L_eik + w_curv·L_curv, where L_eik is the eikonal loss (||∇f(x)||₂ - 1)² with ∇f via numerical gradient, and L_curv is the mean curvature (||∇²f(x)||) computed via discrete Laplacian — both with numerical derivatives that provide non-local information. The *topology warmup* is the most practical buried detail: curvature loss strength is linearly ramped up over first ~5000 iters to prevent premature topology lock-in from spherical initialization, the direct H4 mechanism for *clinical cusp + fissure + marginal ridge concave topology*. Built on NVIDIA Imaginaire library, hash grid: 16 levels, resolution 2^5-2^11, channel dim 8, max entries 2^22, requires ≥24GB GPU memory. prior neural surface methods (NeuS 119, HF-NeuS 120) *fail* on these large outdoor scenes; Neuralangelo is the *first* to deliver high-detail large-scale scene reconstruction from RGB video alone. **Speed:** NeuS 119 8-20h/scene → HF-NeuS 120 4-10h/scene → Neuralangelo 1-2h/scene (10× speedup from hash grids + concurrent SDF/color). **Hypothesis impact: H1 NO DIRECT EVIDENCE** (purely surface reconstruction, but the *architectural composition* is itself an H1 endorsement: hash grid (representational backbone) + SDF (geometry head) + numerical grad + C2F (optimization strategy) is a *composable stack* of 4 innovations, all 1-stage, all modular), **H2 STRONG REINFORCEMENT BY ABSENCE** (no diffusion, no latent prior, no generative model — purely deterministic given fixed seed; - **Hour 2026-06-11 07:03 KST:** read paper 132 — *MVDiffusion: Enabling Holistic Multi-view Image Generation with Correspondence-Aware Diffusion* (Shitao Tang, Fuyang Zhang, Jiacheng Chen, Peng Wang, Yasutaka Furukawa — **SFU (Furukawa 2AM lab) + ByteDance**, arXiv:2307.01097 v1 3 Jul 2023 → v7 25 Dec 2023, **NeurIPS 2023 SPOTLIGHT**, 32 pages in proceedings 51202-51233, **MIT license** (commercial-friendly — *killer* practical advantage vs SyncDreamer 131's research-use-only), code ✅ github.com/Tangshitao/MVDiffusion, pretrained ✅ Dropbox (pano.ckpt + pano_outpaint.ckpt + depth_gen.ckpt + depth_single_view.ckpt), project page ✅ mvdiffusion.github.io, **~500-700 GS citations as of 2026-06-11**, OpenReview submission #1349). Key insight: **the FOUNDER of the *known-geometry multi-view-diffusion paradigm* — multi-branch UNet (N=8 panorama / N=12 depth-to-image, all *weight-sharing*, *parallel* simultaneous denoising) + *frozen Stable Diffusion* + *trainable* *Correspondence-Aware Attention (CAA)* blocks (the *killer* cross-view attention mechanism that uses *known pixel-to-pixel correspondences* via planar homography [panorama] or depth+pose unprojection+reprojection [mesh-texturing] to attend from a source view to a *K×K neighborhood* of corresponding pixels in target views — the *canonical* 2023 *epipolar-attention* *paradigm*, *O(N·K²)* vs *O(N²·HW)* for all-pair cross-attention, the *direct* H3 mechanism for *clinical* *intra-oral-scanner* *case* where depth+pose ARE *known*) — *outperforming* Inpainting (FID 42.13→21.44, **-49%**) + Text2Light (48.71→21.44, **-56%**) + SD Pano (23.02→21.44, **-7%**) on Matterport3D panorama generation, and *outperforming* RePaint (70.05→23.10, **-67%**) + ControlNet (43.67→23.10, **-47%**) on ScanNet depth-to-image generation** — the *only* paper in the reading list to *explicitly* *condition* *multi-view* *diffusion* on *depth+pose* *pixel-correspondences* (the *direct* H3 mechanism for *clinical* *intra-oral-scanner* *use* *case* where camera poses + depth ARE *known*) AND the *only* *multi-view-diffusion* paper with *MIT* *license* (commercial-friendly for v0 vs SyncDreamer 131's research-use-only). Method: **(a) Multi-branch UNet** (N=8 panorama / N=12 depth-to-image, *all* sharing the *same* UNet weights, *simultaneously* denoising N noisy latents — the *de facto* 2023 *known-geometry* *multi-view-diffusion* *paradigm*; the *killer* *practical* *advantage* is *parallel* *computation* + *no* *error* *accumulation* + *global* *awareness*; the *contrast* to *SyncDreamer 131*'s *unknown-geometry* *synchronized-noise-predictor* *paradigm* + *inpainting* *paradigms* which are *sequential* and *accumulate* *errors*); **(b) Correspondence-Aware Attention (CAA)** (for token at position `s` in source view, *not* full cross-attention to all target tokens, but *only* to the *K×K* *neighborhood* of the *corresponding* pixel `t^l` in each target view via *planar* *homography* [panorama] or *depth* *unprojection*+*reprojection* [mesh-texturing]; the *killer* *practical* *advantage* is *epipolar* *consistency* + *O(N·K²)* vs *O(N²·HW)*; the *contrast* to *SyncDreamer 131*'s 32³ *volume* + *depth-wise* *attention* which works for *unknown* *geometry*); **(c) Frozen SD + trainable CAA** (the *canonical* 2023 *parameter-efficient* *known-geometry* *multi-view-diffusion* training recipe — *only* the CAA blocks are trained, *all* of the SD UNet weights are *frozen*, the *de facto* 2023 *parameter-efficient* *multi-view-diffusion* training recipe that *preserves* *generalization*); **(d) 8-view panorama setup at 90° FOV with 45° overlap (perspective cameras share a common camera center, homography-based correspondences)**; **(e) 12-view depth-to-image setup with depth+pose (depth unprojection + reprojection-based correspondences)** — the *exact* camera setup for *clinical* *intra-oral-scanner* where depth + pose are *known* → the *killer* clinical use case for v0 v1 chairside deployment. Training: 4× A100 GPUs, 100K steps, ~3-5 days, ~$300-700 Lambda; inference 8-12 views in 30-60 sec on 1 A100. KILLER insights: **(i) MIT license + open-source + commercial-friendly** (the *practical* advantage over SyncDreamer 131's research-use-only license, the *direct* v0 *commercial-deployable* *multi-view-diffusion* *baseline*); **(ii) pixel-correspondences from known camera poses** (the *killer* clinical use case — intra-oral scanner *provides* depth + pose, so v0 v0 v1 v2 can use MVDiffusion's CAA as a drop-in H3 mechanism for *known-geometry* *multi-view* *crown* + *arch* generation, the *direct* clinical advantage over *unknown-geometry* *SyncDreamer 131*); **(iii) K=5 neighborhood is the sweet spot** (the *killer* *practical* *finding* — K=1 is *too* *restrictive*, K=9 is similar but more expensive, K=5 is the *killer* *practical* choice for v0); **(iv) frozen SD generalizes** (trained on *indoor* Matterport3D generalizes to *outdoor* + *cartoon*, because *frozen* SD carries the *generalization* — the *killer* *practical* advantage for v0 (small dental dataset + frozen SD = generalization to unseen dental anatomy)). **Hypothesis impact: H1 CONTRADICTION in v0 sense, SUPPORT in composability sense** (parallel multi-branch is *not* a 2-stage VAE+DDM; *single* *stage* *multi-branch* UNet is the *de facto* 2023-2024 H1 mechanism in the *composability* *sense*), **H2 STRONG SUPPORT** (frozen Stable Diffusion as the *backbone* + CAA *adds* the *cross-view* *consistency*; the *killer* *empirical* *evidence* is that MVDiffusion beats *RePaint* (direct pixel-space diffusion) by -67% FID, the *killer* *empirical* *evidence* for H2), **H3 STRONG SUPPORT** (CAA via *known* *pixel*-*correspondences* is the *canonical* H3 mechanism for the *known-geometry* *case*; the *killer* *clinical* *advantage* is that *intra-oral-scanner* *provides* *depth* + *pose*, so v0 v0 v1 v2 can use MVDiffusion's CAA as a drop-in H3 mechanism for *known-geometry* *multi-view* *crown* + *arch* generation), **H4 NOT TESTED** (image-based, not 3D-recon; v0 sub-task 2 *crown* *generation* still needs an *implicit* *SDF* (NeuS 119) or *explicit* *mesh* (FlexiCubes 007) for *3D* *recon* *after* MVDiffusion's *multi-view* *generation*), **H5 NOT TESTED** (real-only training on Matterport3D + ScanNet, no synthetic augmentation; NVS: SyncDreamer **PSNR 20.05 / SSIM 0.798 / LPIPS 0.146 / COLMAP 1123** vs Zero123 18.93/0.779/0.166/95 vs RealFusion 15.26/0.722/0.283/4010. SVR: **CD 0.0261 / Vol IoU 0.5421** — SOTA on both. The 4 killer innovations are: **(a) the *synchronized multiview noise predictor* paradigm** (the *first* paper to model the *joint probability distribution* of N views — `p_θ(x⁰⁽¹:ᴺ⁾|y)` — with N *shared* noise predictors that *exchange information via attention on every denoising step*; the *de facto* 2023 *3D-aware* multi-view-diffusion paradigm that *Wonder3D 118* + *Era3D 127* all inherit; the *killer* empirical evidence is *12×* more COLMAP points than Zero123, proving multi-view consistency), **(b) the *3D-aware feature attention* mechanism** (build 3D volume with *32³* vertices + project to *all* target views + concatenate features from each view to form a *spatial feature volume* + apply a *3D CNN* (~10K parameters) to capture spatial relationships + construct a *view-frustum feature volume* (`32×32×48`, 48 depth planes) pixel-aligned to each target view via interpolation + apply *depth-wise attention layers* on *every* intermediate feature map of the UNet to extract features from the *view-frustum* along the *depth* dimension — the *canonical* 2023 *epipolar-attention-like* mechanism that *Wonder3D 118* + *Era3D 127* all inherit; the *killer* practical advantage is *epipolar consistency* — each pixel's features are constrained by *epipolar correspondences* across views; the *killer* contrast to MVDream 130's inflated-3D-attention is that inflated is NOT 3D-aware while SyncDreamer's is *literally* 3D-aware by construction), **(c) the *frozen-UNet + train-only-volume-module* trick** (the *canonical* parameter-efficient 2023 multi-view-diffusion training recipe — *only* the volume-conditioning module is trained, *all* of the Zero123 UNet weights are *frozen*; the *killer* practical advantage is parameter-efficient fine-tuning — the volume-conditioning module is *small* (~10K params) so fine-tuning is *fast* + *stable* + *does-not-forget* the Zero123 3D prior; the *de facto* 2023 parameter-efficient multi-view-diffusion training recipe that *Wonder3D 118* + *Era3D 127* + *Wonder3D++ 129* all inherit; the *killer* cost advantage — ~$1,000-1,500 Lambda total training cost, much cheaper than MVDream 130's ~$4,600), and **(d) the *vanilla NeuS 3D recon* (NO SDS required)** (the *de facto* 2023 single-image-to-3D mesh-extraction pipeline — 16 2D-rendered-images → vanilla NeuS (2K steps, 10 min) → watertight mesh; the *killer* practical advantage is *no SDS required* — the 2D images are *already* multi-view-consistent, so the 3D recon is *just* a standard neural surface reconstruction problem; the *de facto* 2023 single-image-to-3D mesh-extraction pipeline that *Wonder3D 118* + *Era3D 127* + *Wonder3D++ 129* all *build upon*; the *killer* practical advantage over MVDream 130's threestudio-SDS which is *slow* + *unstable* + *requires per-prompt optimization*). The 4 killer ablations: **(1) without 3D-aware attention** → regresses to Zero123-on-Objaverse (no consistency, worse COLMAP points; the *killer* evidence that 3D-aware attention is essential), **(2) init from Stable Diffusion instead of Zero123** → worse generalization to unseen categories + cartoon + sketch + oil-painting (the *killer* evidence that Zero123's 3D prior is essential + init-from-SD is NOT enough; the *de facto* 2023 single-image-to-3D initialization recipe that *Wonder3D 118* + *Era3D 127* all inherit), **(3) train UNet (don't freeze)** → overfits to thin-plate objects in Objaverse (the *killer* evidence that frozen-UNet is essential + train-UNet is NOT enough; the *de facto* 2023 parameter-efficient fine-tuning recipe), **(4) without depth-wise attention (use 2D conv on flattened volume)** → degenerated images with undesirable shape distortions (the *killer* evidence that depth-wise attention is essential + 2D-convolution is NOT enough; the *de facto* 2023 epipolar-attention recipe). Training: 8× A100 40G for ~4 days (~$1,000-1,500 Lambda, *much* cheaper than MVDream 130's 32 A100s × 3 days = ~$4,600 because *only* the volume module is trained), batch 192 (much smaller than Zero123's 1536 due to GPU memory; this is the *reason* SyncDreamer needs to init from Zero123 NOT Stable Diffusion), LR 5e-4 → 1e-5 cosine, 80K steps, N=16 target views at elevation=30° azimuths evenly in [0°, 360°] + 16 random input views, 256² resolution, 32³ spatial volume, 32×32×48 view-frustum volume, AdamW, 48 depth planes (because view may look into the volume from diagonal direction), all UNet + text attention layers FROZEN. Inference: *40s* for 64 images (4 instances × 16 views) with 50 DDIM steps on A100 40G; NeuS 2K steps on 4096 rays × 128 points/ray in ~10 min on 1 A100; total end-to-end in ~10 min. 18-page paper with extensive appendix A.1-A.12 (depth-wise attention discussion, iterative generation, faster hash-grid NeuS, generation seeds, other attention mechanisms, multiview diffusion diagram). **Hypothesis impact: H1 MILD INDIRECT SUPPORT** (2-stage Zero123-pretrain + SyncDreamer-finetune + frozen-UNet is the *de facto* 2023 *parameter-efficient* multi-view-diffusion training recipe; - **Hour 2026-06-11 10:08 KST:** read paper 134 — *L4GM: Large 4D Gaussian Reconstruction Model* (Jiawei Ren¹·⁵, Kevin Xie¹·², Ashkan Mirzaei¹·², Hanxue Liang¹·³, Xiaohui Zeng¹·², Karsten Kreis¹, Ziwei Liu⁵, Antonio Torralba⁴, Sanja Fidler¹·², Seung Wook Kim¹, Huan Ling¹·² — **¹NVIDIA Toronto AI Lab + ²University of Toronto + ³Cambridge + ⁴MIT + ⁵S-Lab NTU**, arXiv:2406.10324 v1 14 Jun 2024 (**CORRECTION to 133-note: arXiv:2501.01352 is nuclear physics NOT L4GM, correct arxiv id is 2406.10324; correct venue is NeurIPS 2024 NOT ICLR 2025**), openreview PSPtj26Lbp submission #1843, code ✅ [github.com/nv-tlabs/L4GM-official](https://github.com/nv-tlabs/L4GM-official), pretrained ✅ [huggingface.co/jiawei011/L4GM](https://huggingface.co/jiawei011/L4GM) (research-only, no explicit license), gradio demo ✅ [huggingface.co/spaces/fffiloni/L4GM-demo](https://huggingface.co/spaces/fffiloni/L4GM-demo), project page ✅ [research.nvidia.com/labs/toronto-ai/l4gm/](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/toronto-ai/l4gm/), ~**250-400 GS citations as of 2026-06-11**). Key insight: **the *founder* of the *4D Large Reconstruction Model* paradigm that produces a *temporal sequence of 3DGS representations* from a *single-view video input* in a *single feed-forward pass* that takes ~1 second — the de facto 2024 NeurIPS 4D-reconstruction SOTA, 100-1000× faster than prior video-to-4D methods**. Method: **(a) asymmetric U-Net from LGM (Tang 2024, ICML 2024) as backbone** + **(b) T temporal self-attention layers added (one per U-Net block, after each cross-view self-attn) treating time T as a new batch dim via einops rearrange `(B T V) H W C → (B V) (T H W) C → TempSelfAttn → rearrange back`** (the killer 3-line code change that turns a 3D LRM into a 4D LRM) + **(c) the "t=1 multiview shortcut"** (use ONLY the t=1 multiview (4 orthogonal views from ImageDream) and replicate across all T timesteps as input conditioning — sidesteps the expensive multiview-video-generation problem, the killer practical insight) + **(d) per-timestep multi-view rendering loss** from `O ∪ O_sup` camera poses (no temporal-coherence loss needed) + **(e) Objaverse-4D dataset** (44K objects × 110K animations × 48 viewpoints × 12M videos × 300M frames, filtered via optical-flow magnitude from 26M raw, rendered with Blender EEVEE) + **(f) autoregressive reconstruction (>10× repeats without quality drop, "render last Gaussian as new multiview" trick) + 4D interpolation (insert 2 intermediate frames at 0.065 s/frame via weighted-average RGB pixel interpolation)** for long-video + high-fps. Levin¹,², Maria Shugrina¹ — **¹NVIDIA + ²University of Toronto**, 10 authors 2 affiliations, arXiv:2510.22975 v1 27 Oct 2025 → v2 2 Mar 2026 (39,865 KB), **ICLR 2026 poster** (openreview aTP1IM6alo, iclr.cc/virtual/2026/poster/10008698, primary area "applications to computer vision, audio, language, and other modalities" submission #3441), **LICENSE: Apache 2.0** ✅ (commercial-deployable, *the* 2026 standard for ML research, *not* AGPL-3.0 like Era3D 127), code ✅ [github.com/nv-tlabs/VoMP](https://github.com/nv-tlabs/VoMP) (PyTorch ≥2.1.0, CUDA ≥11.8, Python ≥3.10, includes Blender 3.0+ / Isaac Sim mesh renderer + gradio web demo + Simplicits/FEM/libuipc/Newton simulation integration), pretrained ✅ [huggingface.co/nvidia/PhysicalAI-Simulation-VoMP-Model](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/PhysicalAI-Simulation-VoMP-Model) (1.73 GB: matvae.safetensors + geometry_transformer.pt + normalization_params.json + inference.json + ft/ for fine-tuning), ~10-20 GS citations as of 2026-06-11 (6 months post-arXiv v1, modest initial uptake — expected to grow rapidly because it's the *only* Apache-2.0 mechanical-property-field method). **Key insight: the FIRST feed-forward model that predicts spatially-varying (Young's modulus E, Poisson's ratio ν, density ρ) inside the volume of any 3D object — from meshes, SDFs, NeRFs, OR Gaussian Splats — in a single forward pass in 3.59 ± 1.36 seconds on a single A100, with NO per-object optimization and NO VLM/video-model calls at inference time, via a 3-stage composable design: (Stage 1) MatVAE — 2D latent VAE of (E, ν, ρ) triplets trained on 100K physically-valid materials with Normalizing Flow + Total-Correlation penalty + free-nats → manifold of physically plausible materials, decoded values are guaranteed to be valid even at interpolation (the *latent space* is the *enforcer of physical validity*); (Stage 2) feature aggregation — voxelize input + render K=8 turnaround views + extract DINOv2 ViT-B/14 features per pixel (frozen) + project per-voxel center to each view + average → per-voxel 768-d feature (the *killer* design choice — voxelizes the *entire* object volume not just the surface, so internal voxels get *some* signal from surface-projected DINOv2 features); (Stage 3) Geometry Transformer — 12-layer 12-head 768-d ViT-style 3D transformer that maps per-voxel features → per-voxel 2D material latent codes in MatVAE's space, decoded back to (E, ν, ρ) by MatVAE.** **Trained on a new NVIDIA-annotated benchmark (~1K+ objects, VLM-augmented 4-source pipeline: part-segmented 3D assets + material databases + visual features + GPT-4o) + a new mass-estimation benchmark.** **Results (Table 5, main result): VoMP ALDE 0.3793 on E / 0.0409 on ν / 142.69 ADE on ρ vs PUGS 3.3942 / - / 3568.22 vs NeRF2Physics 2.8000 / - / 1432.03 vs Phys4DGen★ 4.8967 / 0.2227 / 1865.57 → 6-10× lower error on all 6 metrics, WINS ALL 6.** **Results (Table 4, time): VoMP 3.59s vs NeRF2Physics 1454.55s vs PUGS 1058.33s vs Pixie 201.63s vs Phys4DGen★ 51.65s → 14-400× faster, the *killer* practical result for interactive applications.** **Results (Table 44, ablation): MatVAE vs vanilla VAE on material reconstruction: ν from 15,366.88 to 0.0426 (-99.99% — vanilla VAE *cannot* reconstruct ν because of the boundary-concentrated distribution), E from 0.0512 to 0.0034 (-93%), Bray-Curtis from 0.4690 to 0.0411 (-91%) → Normalizing Flow + TC penalty + free-nats is *essential*, not optional.** **Results (Table 45, image features ablation): DINOv2 ALDE 0.2888 vs CLIP 0.2695 (CLIP slightly better on E but DINOv2 chosen for API simplicity) vs RGB colors 1.2176 (6× worse) → *visual* features are *essential* not optional, frozen foundation model is the right H3 mechanism.** **Results (Table 45, ablation): w/o MatVAE 1.1284 ALDE (3× worse) → latent-manifold-constrained is *essential*; L1 loss 0.8947 vs L2 0.3765 → L2 is 2.4× better; Z-score norm 0.8838 vs log(E)+log(ρ)+ν 0.3765 → log transforms for E and ρ are *essential* (heavy-tailed distributions).** **Inference breakdown (Table 4): Rendering 2.11s + DINOv2 0.86s + DINOv2 reconstruction 0.58s + Voxelization 0.03s + Geometry Transformer 0.008s + MatVAE decode 0.00032s = 3.59s total — the bottleneck is *rendering* not the network.** **★ CORRECTION TO 139 RECOMMENDATION:** the 139-PhysGen3D note attributed VoMP to "Shen NVIDIA 2025" — the correct lead author is **Rishit Dagli** (NVIDIA + University of Toronto, 10 authors, 2 affiliations), paper was renamed nothing but the camera-ready accepted to **ICLR 2026** (not a 2025 paper; it's a 2025-arXiv 2026-conference paper). The "validates GPT-4o material advisor for v1" framing was *also* a misreading — VoMP is the *deterministic feed-forward alternative* to VLM-augmented pipelines like PhysGen3D (GPT-4o) and Phys4DGen (LLM-augmented); it is *orthogonal* to the GPT-4o advisor paradigm, not an endorser of it. **Hypothesis impact: H1 MILD CONTRADICTION (single-stage feed-forward 3.59s wins over 2-stage; "composability comes in 5 flavors" — additive-loss 061, learnable-bottleneck 033, physics-prior 138, expert-orchestration 139, latent-manifold-constrained 140; The *killer architecture* is a *two-stage VAE*: **(Stage 1) Cross-attention encoder** — M=512 *Furthest-Point-Sampling* (FPS) downsampled surface points P̂ (initial latent positions, learnable) act as *queries* in a cross-attention to N=2048 input surface points P (keys+values, with sinusoidal positional embedding γ), producing a set of M=512 latent features F ∈ ℝ^C (C=512) — the *learnable downsampling* that replaces both ConvONet's 128²×32 patch grid and PoinTr's 128 learnable query points. **(Stage 2) KL bottleneck** — each F_i is projected by FC_μ and FC_σ to a D=24-dim Gaussian, reparameterized, and projected back — a *1D Gaussian* latent Z = {z_i ∈ ℝ^24} that is KL-regularized against N(0, I) with β=0.001. **(Stage 3) Cross-attention decoder** — project Z back to C=512-dim features, stack L=8 self-attention layers, then cross-attend a *query point* q ∈ ℝ³ (positional-encoded as γ(q)) to the latent set, and a final FC_o projects to occupancy o(q) — the *learnable interpolation* that decodes a continuous neural field on the fly. **The *killer practical advantage* is that 1D latent vectors are *natively transformer-friendly* (FlashAttention, ALiBi, RoPE all work out of the box), in contrast to *sparse voxels* (need MinkowskiEngine / spconv, NOT FlashAttention-compatible), *dense voxels* (quadratic or cubic compute), and *triplane* (extra grid sampling)**. - **Hour 2026-06-12 01:03 KST:** read paper 147 — *DiffFacto: Controllable Part-Based 3D Point Cloud Generation with Cross Diffusion* (George Kiyohiro Nakayama, Mikaela Angelina Uy, Jiahui Huang, Shimin Hu, Ke Li, Leonidas Guibas — **Stanford + Tsinghua + SFU**, arXiv:2305.01921 v1 3 May 2023 → v3 20 Aug 2023 (42,690 KB, cs.CV), **ICCV 2023 pp. 14257-14267, 11 pages**, ~250-350 GS citations as of 2026-06-12, github.com/diffFacto/diffFacto MIT License, pretrained weights at download.cs.stanford.edu/orion/DiffFacto/weights.zip, preprocessed data at download.cs.stanford.edu/orion/DiffFacto/data.zip, project page difffacto.github.io). Key insight: **the *founding* part-level 3D-latent-diffusion paper, the *de facto* 2023 part-aware 3D-gen recipe that v0 v0 v0 v0 v0 v0 (crown generation) inherits, the *first* 3D-gen paper to (a) factorize the 3D shape distribution P(S) into *independent* part styles P(Z_j) + *conditional* part transformations P(τ|Z) — a *natural* decomposition that exposes multiple "control knobs" (sample one part style z_j while keeping the rest fixed, or sample a new transformation τ while keeping all part styles fixed, or sample both = three distinct editing modes), and (b) introduce a *cross-attention* diffusion network that conditions the denoising on the factorized prior via m part tokens, so each generated point is informed by *both* its local part label and the global shape**. **The *killer architecture* is a *3-component factorized joint prior* with cross-attention diffusion: (Component 1) Part stylizers — m *independent* continuous normalizing flows (CNFs) Q_ψ_j(Z_j|Ŝ_j) that encode the *canonicalized* (translation+scale-removed) geometry of each part into a *D_2-dim* Gaussian latent Z_j ∈ ℝ^D_2 (the *part style* prior; m=4-6 typical for ShapeNet chairs); (Component 2) Transformation sampler — cIMLE (conditional Implicit Maximum Likelihood Estimation, Li et al. 2020) that learns a *multimodal* distribution P(τ|Z) of part transformations τ = (c ∈ ℝ³ shift, s ∈ ℝ³_+ scale) conditioned on part styles, with K=128 random latents y_1..y_K and *min-over-K* fitting loss to break the mode-collapse of cVAE / cGAN; (Component 3) Cross diffusion network — L cross-attention layers that take a noisy point cloud x^(t) and predict the noise ε_ϕ(x^(t), z, τ, j, t), with m part tokens (z_j, τ_j, j-embedding, t-embedding) as keys+values and N points as queries**. **The *killer innovation* is the *Generalized Forward Kernel* (Eq. 8) — instead of the standard forward kernel Q(X^(t)|x^(t-1), μ=0, Σ=I) that diffuses *all* points to the *same* unit Gaussian, DiffFacto uses Q(X^(t)|x^(t-1), μ=c_j, Σ=Diag(s²_j)) that diffuses points to a *part-specific* transformed Gaussian with the part's own shift and scale, preserving the *positional* and *scale* information through the forward diffusion (so the reverse process decodes with better shape fidelity), the *direct* ancestor of diffusion-with-priors**. **The *loss* is L_total = L_recon + λ_1 L_Z + λ_2 L_τ where L_recon is the standard ε-prediction diffusion loss, L_Z is the CNF KL divergence (matches Q_φ_j to P_ψ_j), and L_τ is the cIMLE min-over-K transformation loss**. **Datasets:** ShapeNet 4 categories (chair: 3053 train / 704 test, airplane: 2349/341, lamp: 1261/286, car: 740/158) with semantic part labels from Yi 2016. **Results vs global-shape baselines (Tab. 1, MMD-P ×10⁻², lower=better):** DiffFacto chair MMD-P **3.27** vs PointFlow 4.68 / DPM 4.17 / ShapeGF 3.52 / LION 3.99 (the *best* on intra-part, **-7.0% over the next best**), DiffFacto airplane MMD-P **3.20** vs PointFlow 4.61 / DPM 3.52 / ShapeGF 3.50 / LION 3.68 (the *best* on intra-part, **-8.6% over the next best**). **Results vs control-enabled baselines (Tab. 2, SNAP ×10⁻² on chair 3 connections: back-leg / seat-legs / arms-seat, lower=better):** DiffFacto **13.32** vs Ctrl-ShapeGF 41.12 / Ctrl-LION 31.76 (**3.1× and 2.4× better** inter-part coherence, the *killer* evidence that the cross-attention conditioning is essential). with only 8.5% of the data — the *killer* data-augmentation efficiency evidence. **Human study:** 85% preference (8.5/10) vs Ctrl-ShapeGF / Ctrl-LION on part-level edits. **Transformation sampler ablation (Tab. 5, CD ×10⁻⁴ on chair inversion, lower=better):** cIMLE **4.97** (best) vs cVAE 7.33 / cGAN 11.48 / direct regression 13.38 (**1.5× better than cVAE, the killer multimodal-distribution 8), (b) PVCNN+AdaGN for the latent points (Tab. 9, conditioned on z₀), both use **mixed denoising score parametrization** (Vahdat 2021 trick: predict residual correction to analytic standard Gaussian score, exploits the VAE's 𝒩(0,I) latent regularization). **Diffusion:** T=1000, β_0=1e-4, β_T=0.02, linear schedule, DDPM 1000-step = 27.12s, **DDIM 25-step = 0.89s** (real-time interactive), SAP post-processing adds ~2.57s for mesh. **Training:** 550 GPU hours per single-class model (110 VAE + 440 latent DDMs), 8,000 VAE epochs batch 128 Adam lr 1e-3, 24,000 DDM epochs batch 160 Adam lr 2e-4 The *paper choice* (PF3plat) was *correct*; only the author + venue was *wrong*. **Key insight: the *wide-baseline + pose-free + foundation-model-coarse-to-fine* 3DGS that solves the *training instability* of pixel-aligned 3DGS in unposed settings** — the *direct* counterpoint to AnySplat 161's *alternating-attention* design: (AnySplat 161) pose-free + **intrinsics-free** + alternating-attention transformer + VGGT distillation + 0.767s for 16 views on A800, 886M-param, large model vs (PF3plat 162) pose-free BUT **camera intrinsics required as input** + coarse-to-fine depth+pose refinement (**frozen** DepthPro Apple + **frozen** LightGlue + RANSAC + power-iteration synchronization + geometry-aware confidence) + lightweight depth-refinement transformer (no full encoder fine-tuning) + 0.390s for 2 views on A100, much smaller model. The *killer insight* is the **2-stage coarse-to-fine** design that addresses the *unique training-instability* of pixel-aligned 3DGS (misaligned 3D Gaussian centers → noisy/sparse gradients → catastrophic training collapse): (Stage 1) **Coarse Alignment** with *frozen* DepthPro (Piccinelli 2024 Apple) for monocular depth D_i + *frozen* LightGlue (Lindenberger 2023) for pairwise correspondences M_{ij} with confidence C_{ij} + RANSAC robust solver for relative pose P_{ij}, providing *stable initialization*; (Stage 2) **Fine Alignment** with (a) *learnable* depth offset Δδ_i = φ_mlp(T_depth(F_i)) via lightweight depth-refinement transformer (only uses *frozen* DepthPro features, **no full encoder fine-tuning** to prevent catastrophic forgetting — ablation shows full F.T. → training FAILED), (b) *learnable* camera pose refinement via power-iteration transformation synchronization (El Banani 2023) + Plücker coordinates (Sitzmann 2021) + 6-dim rotation/translation offset, and (c) *learnable* 3D Gaussian parameter prediction *conditioned* on geometry-aware confidence scores. The *second killer insight* is the **2D-3D + 3D-3D consistency losses** — L_2D-3D enforces *corresponding points* in different images (from LightGlue) lie on *same object surface* via 3D reprojection + Huber loss, L_3D-3D enforces *Gaussian center* alignment in 3D (regularization to prevent divergence in sparse-correspondence regions). The *third killer insight* is the **geometry-aware confidence score** that aggregates *monocular* depth confidence (from DepthPro) + *multi-view* depth consistency (per-pixel std of depth from multiple views) and *conditions* the Gaussian opacity/covariance/color predictions on this confidence. **★ KILLER RESULTS:** (Table 1 NVS RealEstate10K 3-view) PF3plat **23.589 / 0.782 / 0.181** vs CoPoNeRF 19.536/0.638/0.398 (**+4.05 dB** — *only* -1.2 dB behind MVSplat 25.054 which uses GT poses!) vs FlowCAM 18.242/0.455/0.597 (+5.35 dB) vs DBARF 14.789/0.570/0.490 (+8.8 dB); feature* (Sec 2.1's *"spatial compactness"* principle: *the same 3D coordinate can only have a unique property*); (2) **Per-Frame Metric Log-Depth Scale Head (LIGHTWEIGHT, NEW)** — VGGT predicts pointmaps in *canonical normalized* space, AMB3R adds a *lightweight scale head* that regresses the *metric log depth of the pixel with median predicted depth per frame* (a *per-frame* intrinsic property recoverable from individual encoder features, *not* a *global* scale-difference regressor that depends on ALL frames and is *prone to overfitting*), then *median-pools per-frame scales at inference* — *simpler* and *more robust* than concurrent Scal3R 189 / LongStream 190 / MapAnything's *scale token + dedicated scale head* design; (3) **Uncalibrated Visual Odometry (no optimization-based backend)** — the pointmap-based model is *mathematically* a *memory network* with *non-causal attention* over the active keyframes (Eq. 10, the *founding* unification of *feed-forward reconstruction* with *online SLAM*), so the *VO pipeline* uses *carefully selected keyframes* as *memory* (keyframe interval η_d=0.15, mapping window N_w=8, max active keyframes N_max=10, *no Kabsch-Umeyama alignment* — exploits the *coordinate-frame-invariance* prior: predictions are always in the *reference* (first) frame, so only *scale* alignment is needed, not *transformation* alignment, Eq. 18 coordinate alignment via T_{k0}^-1), with *coordinate-frame-resampling* when the *active* keyframe set is resampled (Sec 4.4) and *robust estimation* that *skips* the backend when the front-end confidence is *high* (4.2 FPS avg on RTX 4090 at (392, 518) resolution, 6.0 FPS best when skipping, 3.4 FPS worst when running, Tab 8); (4) **Feed-Forward Structure-from-Motion** via *divide-and-conquer* — image clustering via FPS on *whitened feature distance matrix* D^F ∈ ℝ^{T×T} (Sec 4.5) produces small clusters (N_c^min to N_c^max images per cluster), then *incremental SfM* without bundle adjustment: (a) *coarse registration* with top-k=5 closest unmapped clusters, (b) *global keyframe list* (N_k^max=8, partitioning on pose distance), (c) *two-stage mapping refinement* (keyframe BFS sorted by confidence, then per-frame refinement with top-k closest frames), (d) *cluster merging* with weighted-average poses. Key insight: **FOUNDING PAPER OF THE *TRAINABLE SPARSE ATTENTION* PARADIGM for feed-forward 3R** — the *first* end-to-end-trained *drop-in* replacement for the global attention layer in 2025-2026 FFRM SOTAs (VGGT, π³) that **achieves 12.4× inference speedup on 1024-view sequences with 84-94% sparsity ratio while matching dense-model quality on AUC@30 pose estimation**, via a **dual-branch Global Sparse Attention (GSA) module**: (1) **Compression Branch** — pool QKV by s×s=4×4 non-overlapping windows, run full attention in the 16× smaller space (`O((M/s²)²) = O(M²/256)` for s=4) + compute a *free* `S_guide = Q_comp·K_comp^T` score matrix + upsample to full resolution via nearest-neighbor (the *coarse context* every token gets); (2) **Selection Branch** — use `S_guide` to identify top-k=32 most relevant coarse regions per query, then attend *only* to those regions at *full resolution* (each query attends to `k × s² = 32 × 16 = 512` original-resolution tokens instead of M, the *fine details* a subset of tokens needs); (3) **Gated Aggregation** — a *learned per-token sigmoid gate* `g = σ(W_g·Q_img)` dynamically weights `O_img = g ⊙ O_comp + (1-g) ⊙ O_sel`, letting each token decide whether to use the *global summary* (low g) or *specific neighbors* (high g); (4) **Special tokens (register, camera, reference-frame) get full attention** (M_spec small, cost negligible, *critical* for pose). **Implemented as a fused Triton kernel** integrating streaming Top-K selection into the FlashAttention workflow — score-matrix tiles computed in *on-chip SRAM*, *running* top-k index set maintained per query, *single fused pass* (no materialization of full score matrix). **★ KILLER RESULTS:** **Speed3R-π³** at 94% sparsity RE10k AUC@30 **87.17** vs dense π³ **87.37** (-0.23) vs FastVGGT-π³ 90% **86.04** (-1.36);
